To the north, the dead stirred once more, and dire tidings spoke of one of NIGHT’S DARK MASTERS force gathering in the shadows, biding its time.

Large, decisive battles were rare among the warring princes, who favored skirmishes over set piece battles. Realizing the threat north as his brother once did, Vortigern took matters into his own hands, leading most of his force north and calling for allies. Meanwhile, in his absence he entrusted his bannerettes with commanding their own forces, ensuring the city remained secure. The bannerettes found themselves presented with numerous opportunities to demonstrate their tactical acumen on the field of battle to their liege lord and earn his favor and thus bring greater prestige among the nobility. In these small wars they seized every chance to showcase their prowess.

As preparations for the northern campaign commenced in earnest, the marquis moved to ensure that his host was armed not only well equipped with weapons and armor, but that they could fight with every advantage possible. His youth was spent battling the restless dead in Mousillon as his brother had, and this had taught Vortigern the terrible efficacy of divine might against such abominations, and he would not march without it. He therefore issued summons throughout his domains and beyond, calling for clergy devoted to Morr. These priests were not to tend the fallen or grant final rites, but to stand among the living, warding them with sacred blessings and fortifying their spirits against the horrors to come. In this, the marquis aimed to strengthen both the morale and the spiritual resolve of his army. Few Morrians answered his call, yet Vortigern was not disappointed. Those who came did so with fierce devotion, committing themselves fully to the campaign, and they did not come alone. At their side marched their silent Black Guard. Within the newly consecrated Garden of Morr, one among the priests personally blessed the marquis’s blade and armor, sanctifying them for the trials ahead. They further presented him with a banner bearing the raven, sacred sigil of Morr, which was entrusted to his battle standard bearer and would henceforth fly above the host. At the same time, Vortigern commissioned a grand triptych depicting the Lady’s divine guidance of the noble Landuin during his rule of Mousillon. This holy relic was to be taken north with the army, illustrating her guidance that they marched with and that they marched with and fought in accordance with her will.

On the eve of departure, noble and commoner alike gathered in a solemn assembly before the city gates. There, a grail damsel bestowed her ceremonial blessings upon the host. When the rites were complete, Vortigern drew his sword, its sanctified steel catching the light, and at his signal the army set forth, marching north upon beginning the Sontrailles First Crusade against death.

As they marched, they were joined by contingents sent by their allies from Palinam, Rhoytrin, and Philany, all united in their resolve to end the threat once and for all. Night’s dark masters did not sit idly by while the army marched; however, few traveled near their cursed territory without their knowledge and they did not suffer such actions in silence. It wasn’t long before the alliance was descended upon by hordes of the undead. It took two full days to reach the foot of the hills through the heavy fighting and it was there where the true battle began.

Beneath a sunless sky, the abbots raised the sacred triptych high above the ranks, calling upon the soldiers to stand fast. Their voices rang out amid the din of battle as the engines of war answered in kind, hurling volleys of flaming missiles into the advancing mass. Zombies burned and fell, yet still they lurched onward, heedless of flame or ruin.Few among the nobles present had lived to fight at Aedric’s Rest. Vortigern was one of only a handful perhaps who had stood upon those blood-soaked walls in years past. As the battle unfolded, he searched the enemy ranks for the cursed knight who had slain Aedric, seeking vengeance long deferred. Yet no trace of the red armored knights could be found.

Instead, his gaze was drawn to something else. High above the field sat the true master of the host, the dark lord himself, enthroned upon the back of a zombified dragon. Around him rode his retinue of twelve knights clad in macabre black armor, silent and unmoving, watching the slaughter below as one might observe a foregone conclusion. The sky soon darkened as clouds of bats and other winged monstrosities filled the air. Then came the shriek loosed by the vampire lord himself. At its sound, the dead surged forward as one, crashing upon the crusaders’ lines. Hexes and foul sorceries were hurled without cease, black energies ripping through ranks of men. Scores fell screaming, and though the clergy strove mightily, even their prayers could do little to blunt the storm.

It was then that Guilloys, commander of the knights on the left flank, sounded his horn and charged against Vortigern’s orders. Gaudy banners and fluttering pennons burst through the gloom as thunderous hooves drowned out the cries of the dying. Yet no sooner had the knights committed themselves than the earth itself betrayed them. Wraiths and undead clawed their way free of the soil behind the charging lances, severing them from the main line. The reckless charge very nearly sealed the doom of Guilloys and his men, and perhaps that of the entire host. Yet Vortigern swore an oath then and there to save them, whatever the cost. The warriors of Sontrailles and their allies surged forward in desperate disorder, only to find themselves encircled as fresh enemies rose all around. Winged nightmares plunged from the heavens, snatching soldiers from the ground and carrying them screaming into the darkness. Still Guilloys’ knights pressed on. They smashed into the undead ranks, clearing a path through rotting flesh and splintered bone. But grasping hands slowed their advance, dragging riders from their saddles to be torn apart on the ground.

Through this chaos, Vortigern and his personal retinue cut their way forward, hacking through the mire. It was there, amidst the roar of battle, that the dark lord descended, his monstrous mount crushing men beneath claw and wing as it landed before the marquis. What followed has ever since been a matter of fierce debate among scholars and priests.The abbey of the Lady maintains that they beheld her divine intervention, that a true champion strode forth, radiant with fey light, mist curling about his steps, and that all darkness recoiled before him. The cultists of Morr contend instead that it was the sacred runes upon Vortigern’s armor and blade that turned aside foul sorcery and granted him the strength to strike down the vampire lord and three of his black armored knights by his own hand. It is written by chroniclers that:

“Blessed Vortigern’s radiance broke through the mire and his shining blade scattered the darkness from his sight. Such was his strength in arms and skill in battle that in his hour of wrath no fiend would abide him and fled into the shrinking dark.”

Those common soldiers who survived spoke only of this: that the marquis and his personal guard faced the vampires amid the storm of battle, and that when the clash ended, the masters of the dead lay broken. Whatever the truth, the result was beyond dispute. With their lord destroyed, the undead horde collapsed into ruin, crumbling where it stood. And thus, the day was won. They did not have much time to gather the dead or to rest after the battle for they could see upon the hills the dead were beginning to stir once more and a lone figure watched from the heights.

As the crusaders marched their way up the hills it became apparent that the dark lord was not the only foe that held sway on the lands. They spent days cleansing the dark magics from where they stood and hacked and slashed their way against new waves of undead and specters. Even for all their zeal, the small gains they made came at an eye watering price in lives and the allied leaders would decide it was best to fall back. In this way Vortigern’s crusade north ended. He surely realized the enormous efforts it would require to fully cleanse the northern hills, not dissimilar to the errantry war started by Charlen many years ago. However he knew he did not have the strength to do so. As they retreated, they set the battlefield ablaze to hinder pursuit and ensure the dead stayed buried, even after the purification rites. The warriors would return to Sontrailles to cheering crowds and fanfare, regarded as mighty heroes against the darkness north. The morrian would remain at the shrine within the city, given the head of the vampire lord to guard within the catacombs with their lives.

The marquis knew the undead threat to the north would persist throughout his lifetime. In response, he established a voluntary force stationed between the city and the northern hills, where they would serve as a bulwark against the relentless undead menace. Initially many knights volunteered their lances for the defence. A great furnace would be built to burn the mountains of corpses as they were cut down. Though zeal for the bastion was strong, the number of knights volunteering dwindled as the years passed by. As a result, disgraced knights, those who had broken their vows, violated the rules of chivalry, or acted dishonorably, were sent to the bastion. There, they could reclaim their honor and nobility in the eyes of their liege lord by fighting the countless undead in defense of the city. These knights would become known as the Knights Forlorn and their lines the Divide.

In 2488, following the disastrous defeat at Death’s Pass and Morglum Necksnapper’s decree, the orcs returned to menace the borderlands. A host of knights sought refuge in Sontrailles, rallying under the marquis, now known as Vortigern the Blessed. Together, they fought in defense of the region alongside allied princes. He would assign Sir Grimold de Mousillon, a former member of the Knights Forlorn to head a force east to assist the holdings of Halfear’s hold and Sir Guillame de Sontrailles to assist in the defence of the Kingdom of Sarngul. When a druchi army came to despoil the kingdom and carry off their people it was Vortigern who would vanquish their dread lord and drive them back to their ships. For twenty one years the warriors remained steadfast against the orcs and other wild things that once again ravaged with impunity. During this time the marquis would have dreams of terrible import. The city would be reduced to rubble, consumed by a sea of darkness. In preparation for this impending ruin he strengthened the walls, dug trenches, and enforced the training of any boy and man of age to be able to fight among the ranks of Sontrailles. Additionally, he was compelled to complete the catacombs beneath the Shrine of Morr. In the summer of 2509 the great scourge would arrive in the form of the Tamurkhan, the Maggot Lord.

News of a great horde hailing from the north arrived and with it the news that the dwarfs had begun closing their gates and hiding within their great holds. Scarcely a week after the news came the sudden attacks came. The horde quickly splintered and roving warbands burned and despoiled all in their wake. The knights of Sontrailles were hard pressed to withstand the new menace as warbands circumvented the Kingdom of Sarngul ahead of the main army. In his advanced age Vortigern still fought with youthful vigor and himself claimed a good many heads of the dark gods’ champions. Most of the petty lords and their holdings were destroyed without resistance, however, the strongest lords and principalities united to form the Confederation of the Eagle, to which Sontrailles pledged its strength. General Lietpold the Black would gather their forces to meet the Kurgan in open battle. Vortigern knew, with certainty, that this hour had long been foretold. The dreams that had plagued him for years were no idle phantoms but portents, the city was doomed. He ordered the people of Sontrailles to gather what they could and flee while time remained.

His advisors and lieutenants believed retreat was unthinkable and that with his supposed supernal might the city may yet be saved if they defended from behind the walls, however, his decision was final. He would name Evroult d’Aigremont his successor, entrusting him with the journey north and the safekeeping of their people. As the Kingdom of Sarngul fell, the people of Sontrailles began preparing to flee northward. Vortigern gathered a voluntary force to join the Confederation’s forces, hoping to buy his people time. As he donned his panoply of war one last time he was tormented with visions of his city in ruin and its people devastated. Riding to the gate he would pass the garden of Morr knowing he would soon pass into his embrace. As the final rites were administered, he beheld Sir Grimold, alongside his son, a knight errant, assisting the commoners in the last hours of preparation. He would ride out with a small host and join forces with the crusader lords and unite with the rest of the Confederations armies.

The force was naught but a small obstacle for the forces of Tamurkhan and Drazhoath’s legions. Hopelessly outnumbered and outmatched, they did not hold for long. The Knights Forlorn, accustomed to fighting overwhelming odds, fared better than most. Yet, in the end, they were too reduced to a heap of broken bodies and shattered plate. As Vortigern watched Lietpold and his sellswords flee the field, he ordered Sir Bohem to send word to the city of their defeat. Then, he rallied his remaining knights for one final, desperate charge. In a savage drive they fought their way to the favored champion of Nurgle. One by one, they fell before the monstrous champions of Chaos, until only Vortigern remained. Alone, he pressed on, his sword rising and falling as he cut his way through the reeking tide to stand at last before Tamurkhan himself. Alas, even the blessed Vortigern would fall, just like all those who challenged the Maggot Lord before him. As he fell he was gifted one last vision by his silent patron. The city would thrive once again because of the efforts of heroes like Guillaime, Evroult, Grimold, and the next generation. With this comfort Vortigern the Blessed would fall in 2409, his head and banner claimed by Tamurkhan.

entries.title: Sundering of Sontrailles
entries.body:
“.. And so Etienne’s gate was breached and with it our hope crushed. The commoners joined their liege lords in one final stand yet in our hearts we knew there could be no victory. How could there be when our light was extinguished on the field when Lord Vortigern the Blessed fell?..”

 - Excerpt from the historian Oudin’s telling of the destruction of the city, 2409

As heroic as the actions of Vortigern were they did not stave off the warriors of the north for long. A warband, led by the Slaaneshi champion Gorgraoth, rushed feverishly toward Sontrailles. Bohem’s timely arrival gave the populace precious hours of advanced warning. Many were still flooding out of the gates making their way to the Black Mountains, skirting the Geistenmund hills. Evroult had already brought a majority of the populace out of the city when the Kurgan riders were on their heels. The defense of the city fell to Aubin, one of Vortigern’s paladins. With no hope of relief, the gates were sealed shut, and the defenders steeled themselves for a final, doomed stand.

The gatehouse held firm for days against the siege engines of the Dawi Zharr, and under Aubin's command, the enemy was repelled from the walls time and again, despite the overwhelming numbers. On the first day, Aubin slew a mighty daemon and cast its corpse from the wall in triumph, having the blessed triptych raised high for all to see. On the third day, marauders managed to scale the walls in force, only to be thrown off after hours of brutal fighting and heavy casualties. On the fourth day a majority of Sontrailles siege engines were destroyed by the cannons of the Dawi Zharr. On the fifth day a great battering ram of the enemy smashed the gates, Aubin was mortally wounded by a blast of hellcannon fire, and the defenders were forced from the walls, retreating to their prepared positions in the streets to defend against the slaaneshi invaders. Here every citizen fought with desperate resolve against the invaders but they would not hold for more than a handful of hours before they were at the gate of the keep of Aedric’s rest. The streets ran red with blood, while those unfortunate enough to be captured alive were subjected to horrors most profane, others being sent in chains to the dawi zharr. A few sought into the catacombs beneath the city, putting their trust in the holy works of Vortigern. Bohem would meet his end keeping black plate clad warriors at bay on the stairs leading to Aedric’s rest. He would be hacked to pieces before dusk.

With free reign over the city, Gorgraoth dedicated his victory to his fickle patron and engaged in hedonistic revelry in its ruins in a manner most vile for weeks, toying with any survivors found and defiling the Lady’s triptych commissioned by Vortigern. He and his warband ignored Tamurkhan’s call to assault Nuln, instead bickering with the brutal followers of a rival khornate warband led by Korgan over contested territory, while sharpening their blades against the relentless shambling dead that still plagued the northern lands. Some survivors fled the catacombs in search of safety, desperate to escape the torments of the invaders, while others chose to remain hidden in the shadows. They only ventured out from their refuges to scavenge for scraps or fill their bellies with unspeakable fare. It would be years before any righteous souls dared to inhabit Sontrailles once more.

entries.title: Reconquest of the Border Princes and Sontrailles
entries.body:
“.. We will root them from our home, this is the day we take the battle to them, this is the day we correct the course of our history!..”

 - Excerpt of the history of Oudin detailing Evroult de Sontrailles’ speech rallying the men of Sontrailles, Summer 1532 (2510 IC)

When the populace fled the city, the Kurgan riders quickly closed in. In response, several nobles led their charges away from the main column, splintering in different directions, some never reaching their rally point in the Black Mountains. These knights carved out a humble existence, ruling their charges while remaining ever watchful. These small settlements would persevere, fending off Chaos marauders, greenskins, and the countless other dangers that plagued the borderlands. Evroult gathered as many as he could to his mountain settlement, yet the spirit of the people faltered in the face of their grim reality. They believed that the Lady had forsaken them in their darkest hour. When they appealed to the dwarfs of Karak Hirn and other settlements for aid, most kept their holds sealed, choosing to weather the storm of Chaos on their own. Only three smaller settlements, such as the dwarfs of Khazid Dargran, answered the call and marched to battle when the time came. Among the other border princes, Prince Rillian proved the staunchest ally and gathered them to fight besides the banners of Sontrailles. Evroult decided to bide his time, patiently gathering his strength. Some of the other nobles viewed this as cowardice, a betrayal of their chivalric vows, and set out on their own separate missions. Sir Foucault de Mousillon led a doomed rescue attempt to free slaves taken by the Legion of Azorgh, ultimately meeting his end along with the men who followed him. Guillame d'Eitenfort coordinated his efforts with other surviving knights, but his success in freeing their kin from the chains of the Dawi Zharr remained minimal, yet each small victory emboldened their actions. Wracked with grief over his father’s death and the uncertain fate of his son, Grimold de Mousillon took to raiding, launching lightning strikes against the enemy. Yet, his efforts were driven more by vengeance than by rescue. Many of the crusader fiefs fell to Tamurkhan’s onslaught though their remnants remained defiant of the northmen’s occupation. There stood few knights left of Charfourier and those that lived remained an ever present thorn in their side as did many other survivors.

In 2510, one year to the day after the fall of Sontrailles, Evroult gathered his forces and marched down from the mountains alongside his dwarf allies, uniting with the remaining knights of Sontrailles, other crusader states, and the border princes to take back their holdings. Together, they would crush the scattered marauding warbands that had made the borderlands their home. As they liberated towns, their former lords would once again take up their positions of leadership. The initial successes engendered coordinated resistance amongst the warlords and soon the rabble bands joined together unified by common threat under Korgar. Within a league of Mognia the allied army would face the combined host of their foes. The knights of Sontrailles, banners and pennons streaming in the wind, thundered down the slope, lances leveled. At their side, the dwarfs advanced in shielded ranks side by side with the men at arms of Sontrailles. The Border Princes, forming the center with their pike formation and bowmen loosing volleys of arrows. The battle was carnage incarnate. The Chaos warriors, clad in hellplate, met the charge with monstrous strength, their fell blades shattering lances and hewing limbs. Korgar himself waded through the bloodshed proving himself worthy of the prodigious gifts of his patron, his great axe felling knights and dwarfs alike. Evroult met him in single combat, sword ringing against ensorcelled steel, but the Chaos Champion was a force beyond mortal reckoning. With a terrible swing, Korgar shattered the knight’s shield, then drove his axe deep into Evroult’s chest. The lord of Sontrailles fell to his knees, coughing blood, his vision fading as the banner of his house crumpled into the mud. The princes fled into the hills, their banners discarded, their lords slain. Outflanked, the dwarfs were swiftly cut down, and their lord, Svenef Cragcleaver, was the last to fall, atop the bodies of his fallen kin. The knights broke as all was lost.

It was a dark day in a time of sorrow for the people of Sontrailles, for though they had inflicted a heavy toll on the enemy, the Northmen still claimed a pyrrhic victory. The only solace was the recovery of the Raven Banner of Vortigern. By now the former leadership of Sontrailles had been diminished. Now among the senior bannerettes and renewed by his son’s return who had fled the catacombs with morrian priests and civilians, Grimold led the efforts in retaking Sontrailles.

With the loss of many skilled soldiers, the traditional tactics of the knights were no longer effective. It would take time to train new recruits to fight in formation and instill discipline in them needed to do so in the fires of war. He would devise new strategies. He drew inspiration from his northern neighbors, the Empire of Man, adapting their archaic weapon, the war wagon, and modifying its design to suit the unique needs of his theater of war and tactics. He would seek out engineers from Tilea and with them spent countless nights drafting plans, carefully considering every detail of the wagon’s design. Reinforced with heavy timber and plates of thick steel, its wheels crafted for swift maneuvering, and interior large enough to hold men and weapons both and artillery, the war wagon would be both shield and spear, a mobile fortress that leveraged the commoner’s training in siege warfare and allowed them to bring it to open field combat and use their foes natural aggression against them. Dissent brewed among the nobility, many of whom viewed this style of warfare as cowardly. Debates raged in public areas for some time before they were finally persuaded by Grimold’s ideas. While the designs were finalized, the soldiers were drilled in these tactics, practicing with hay carts as the first war wagons were being constructed. Before the year’s end, what many of the common folk dubbed “The Iron Caravan” was ready for war.

Many of the border princes who were allied with the knights of Sontrailles had fled north to the Empire of Man or west to Tilea seeking safer homes after their defeat at Mognia. Others that remained stayed in their retaken liberated homes, content to rule their meager holdings, few would again march to drive out the invaders, foremost being Prince Rillian eager to reclaim his holdings and exact vengeance. Grimold would send his son among a delegation to appeal once again to the dwarfs however they deemed the endeavor foolish, blaming the deaths of their kin in the previous effort on the reckless folly of the manlings, and refused to offer aid, lest more of their own fall to uphold the pride of the knights. With no additional sources of manpower, Grimold gathered all the warriors he could and marched down the mountains, just as Evroult had done the year before.

 With fewer allies, the lord knew that in every battle, they would be outnumbered. Every battle they would set up their wagon forts and fire missiles at the oncoming hordes of chaos and protect their flanks with ranks of pikes and shields. The knights would sally forth from their positions to engage the enemy cavalry and strike out at the enemy with their lances then return to the safety of the wagon forts or protected flanks of pikemen. Considerable effort was required to hold back the knights, many of whom were the sons of fallen nobles from previous conflicts, too young to participate at the time however Grimold and the veteran knights knew for victory to be achieved, restraint was required. Some wagons were outfitted with cannons from Prince Rillian, though Grimold was reluctant to allow it, only relenting because commoner troops were operating them. The daily drills enabled the soldiers to quickly set up and pack the wagons, allowing them to shift from static defensive positions and remain mobile to support the knights when they fully committed to the charge to break the enemy or fall back in a false retreat when necessary. The new tactics proved effective, enabling them to defeat enemy forces often outnumbering them by several times in running battles. Weeks of campaigning allowed homesteads and hamlets in the territories to be liberated from the invaders and once again be inhabited by the displaced. In the summer of 2512 the knights of Sontrailles would have their chance to exact vengeance on the enemy west of the Geistenmund hills. The forces of Korgar and Gorgraoth set aside their personal conflicts, uniting to stand against the knights led by Grimold. On that hot summer’s day the battle was long. Grimold refused to fully commit for hours, instead orchestrating swift, hit and run attacks by his knights. As they retreated, the wagons unleashed relentless volleys upon the pursuing Chaos warriors, steadily whittling down their ranks while executing a controlled withdrawal and allowing the enemy to overextend. As they fell back toward the river, the water at their backs left them with no escape. As the chaos warriors charged toward the wagon forts, Grimold had his banner bearer unfurl the restored Raven Banner and proclaimed that it was time to unleash their fury. The knights flanked and charged full tilt and the infantry smashed into the chaos lines. Steel clashed against steel, shields splintered, and plate was sundered as both sides hurled their full might at one another. The warriors of chaos were trapped between the hammer and anvil. Korgar carved a bloody tribute to Khorne as he bellowed challenges. Gorgraoth would not be outdone by his rival, however, and cleaved his way toward Grimold, who met his challenge head on. The two clashed in a flurry of lightning quick strikes, matching one another blow for blow, over the din of battle the clashing of their blades rang. After a long and exhausting duel between the two champions, Grimold would stand triumphant. The allies would break through, relentlessly grinding down enemy lines, leaving the field strewn with corpses on their way to the city. Korgar was pierced with seven pikes through his body and Prince Rillian’s sword and burned among the others. Under a sky covered with ash, the ruins of Sontrailles stood in eerie silence. The once towering gate lay in ruins. Cracked canals ran dry, and rubble choked the once bustling avenues. The wind carried whispers of ghosts of a lost era, laughter, music, the clang of forges now drowned in ethereal weeping. Fires flickered in the distance as shadows moved through the wreckage, scavenging what remained. It would be years of repair and purification before the city could claim its former glory. In the wake of that final battle, all errant knights were elevated to knights of the realm.

entries.title: Reconstruction and Reign of Grimold
entries.body:
“ If we are to survive, if we are to live to see our children grow and the seasons pass, if we are to endure the coming times then we must change. For what we were will not carry us through what is coming”

 -Words of Grimold de Mousillon as recorded by the historian Oudin, 1535 (2513 IC)

The city was barely habitable, its very essence scarred by the ruinous powers that had passed through. The tormented wails and weeping of suffering souls echoed on the wind. In the old merchant’s district, bodies had fused with wood and stone, contorted into unnatural poses, their agonized expressions forever etched in death. The few who still clung to life were swiftly granted peace. All around, the unchecked vile hedonism of the past could be seen and felt, a lingering stain on the ruins. The people of Sontrailles were accustomed to hardship and immediately began reconstruction efforts as they trickled in. It would not be long before refugees returned to their homelands. The city had to be purified by clerics of various deities, who volunteered their efforts in the ravaged land. It would take years before their work was fully complete. Many of the structures had to be burned and torn down to rid the city of its taint. Ghoulish figures would be seen at night searching for sustenance. These hapless creatures would be hunted and chased to their homes in the catacombs where they would be purged. Grimold for his efforts would be appointed marquis of the city and as his first action would restore the Knights Forlorn, gathering a band of knights under a new banner and sending them north to protect against the undead once more while the city was rebuilt. The knights errants who had been recently dubbed knights of the realm inherited their father’s lands and titles. The lands and titles of nobles whose lineages were extinguished were granted to any second son brave enough to forge their own path, laying the foundation for noble lineages that have endured to the present day. Engineers and laborers would work from dawn to dusk, clearing out debris, breaking apart structures and rebuilding over them for years while the surrounding arable land would again be used to grow foodstuffs.

Tamurkhan’s invasion would leave an indelible mark on Grimold’s mind. The sheer devastation it had caused could never be allowed to happen to their homeland again, he would improve their defences and make reforms. He would build a second higher wall behind the first and outfit the crenellations with cannons. The city would be sectioned by districts by massive walls. There would be hidden trapdoors that the defenders could use to maneuver around the city via a series of tunnels to flank the enemy should they make it in. The designs were made by a Bretonnian engineer of some renown Luc Borseiller who had come at the invitation of the marquis all the way from Paravon. The inclusions of cannons would cause much dismay amongst the nobility. The knights of old Bretonnia did not allow the liberal use of black powder and many saw Grimold’s use of blackpowder in the war wagons and now cannons in the fortifications as a road towards the proliferation of unchivalrous weaponry allowed among the knights and soldiers against the laws of old. Whether true or not, Grimold stockpiled black powder reserves. This tension culminated in a trial by combat, where Guillame challenged Grimold to determine the future of black powder use. Guillame lost the duel but was ultimately spared. Seeing his mercy as an insult and rejecting these changes, Guillame left the city with his followers, heading east toward the Badlands. The rest of the nobility, most of whom were devoted adherents of the Cult of the Lady, took this as a personal insult to their patron. In response, Grimold made a public display of fealty, seeking to mend relations. He gave a half-hearted thanks to the Lady in the shrine within the ruins of Aedric’s Rest while the reinstated grail pilgrims gave sermons in praise of the Lady’s grace and her role in their grand victory. To further placate the nobility he modified the law set in place by Ramnulf that would prohibit nobles and those in “good stations” to wield black powder weapons, relegating it only to those in lower status, furthering that those that have used such weapons would be unable to own land and pay a single payment tax for the privilege. This had the intended effect and the nobility were mollified. He would however also grant endowments to smiths and other craftsmen who would improve designs, including to black powder weapons, improving designs of weapons and armor.

During this tumultuous time, the Baron of Aubagne-sur-Grismerie sent a delegation to the newly appointed Marquis for soldiers in his war against a rival lord. Even during these evil times, Grimold felt it was his duty to honor his absentee liege lord’s request. Thus, he would send a small contingent of knights and soldiers to make the perilous journey to Mousillon. Among them would be his son, Armand.

The expenses of the reconstruction were mounting. Promised payments to the engineers who had designed the great walls and war wagons, along with countless other obligations, soon revealed the treasury to be wanting. Thus, the old tolls were reestablished, and the marquis himself underwrote merchant ventures through promissory notes, ensuring that Sontrailles might be stocked with goods drawn from the wider Borderlands and from realms beyond. Merchants bound for Bretonnia were also charged with a secondary task, to carry word to wandering knights that those seeking adventure and glory in the wildlands should look to Sontrailles. In time, this call drew many errant knights and exiled nobles in search of a new lord and a worthy cause. Through these measures, coin once more flowed through the city, and seasoned warriors swelled its ranks. Yet the greatest yield came not from tolls or trade, but from the hills themselves. The Geistenmund Hills proved rich in ore of exceptional quality. From these veins, the smiths of the Durocher family had forged their renowned Virtuous Steel. The mines were reopened, producing iron, silver, and other metals in abundance. The silver alone funded many of the city’s works, and in due course, the marquis’s debts were repaid in full.

Relations between the old and new Border Princes remained peaceful for a time, yet the duplicitous nature of some soon rekindled hostilities. Many lords were slaughtered in the invasion, leaving territories unclaimed and borders disputed and with them old grievances reignited. In the absence of a unifying enemy, the princes turned upon one another, and Grimold led armies against neighboring territories. Such was the devastation, still fresh from the horrors of the Northmen’s invasion, that they were soon compelled to seek peace, to preserve both their people and their own lives.

From this uneasy peace arose a series of non-aggression pacts, and after a council of the reigning lords, the Northern Border Confederacy was established. This alliance brought together the principalities east of the Lagoon of Tears and west of the Forest of Gloom, with Akendorf, Brovska, and Munzig standing as founding members.

In a similar vein Grimold sought to reconcile with the dwarfs of Khazid Dargran and the surrounding dwarfs as they lay blame on the death of Svenef Cragcleaver on the pride of the Evroult and thus refused Sontrailles’ friendship declaring them unworthy, seeing them as worse allies than Bretonnians in the west. As a token gesture Grimold had ten casks of Sontrallais wine sent to the new lord of Karak Grentaz, Furgil Stonebrow who refused them sending the envoys back with insults, particularly calling the vintage “swill” among other heinous and vile abuses hurled towards the Marquis. Unwilling to stomach the disparagement from a lesser breed when his hand was offered in friendship, Grimold declared war on Khazid Dargran and its allies and so the War of Wine began. In truth the war consisted of only two battles, with Sontrailles prevailing against the dwarfs in one and being driven from the field in the second. Grimold would challenge Furgil personally, wishing to decide the outcome of the war in a duel which the dawi lord accepted, unwilling to insult his storied clan and even wagered a hefty sum of gold, silver, and trinkets against a vault of the Marquis’. It is recorded that the duel lasted half an hour and that Grimold drove Furgil to a knee, then offered mercy only to be spat at. Furgil Stonebrow’s head would be severed clean from his body. While no more retaliatory strikes were made by the dawi who wished to uphold Furgil’s honor, it is rumored Grimold’s name is written in the book of grudges of Khazid Dargran and it would be decades before Sontrailles could make meaningful relations with the dwarfs of the Black Mountains.

Of all the crusader states that Charlen’s errantry established in the region, Sontrailles had weathered the storm of Tamurkhan better than any other. Its walls were repaired, its banners flew once more, and its people returned soon after Grimold’s victory. In the years that followed the victory, the surrounding remnants of the crusader fiefs rebuilt as Sontrailles did, yet for most their strength was diminished, and one by one they turned toward Sontrailles. Some came as supplicants, others as wary equals, but believed that alone they would fall. One by one the surviving states joined themselves to Sontrailles by oath as brethren and together they would join the Northern Border Confederacy as one.

This unification was not only brought about by kinship and regional threats for the shadow of the north still loomed long after they were expunged from the lands. Dark portents spread across the Borderlands since the scouring of the invaders. In those days northmen captives boasted of another son of the Great Kurgan, a warlord fated to march south with a host mightier than the Maggot Lord’s, and that he was only one. There were to be four in total, a champion of each of the disgusting gods of the north, all leading mightier hosts than the preceding one, each a herald for the end. The priests of Morr spoke more cautiously, warning that such tales often preceded great harvests of souls. The servants of the Lady claimed the portents were trials set before the faithful, meant to temper the righteous and reveal those worthy to stand when the storm finally broke such as when the Maggot Lord arrived, for indeed Vortigern the Blessed was one such worthy, having supped from the grail. Many believed this second invasion would come soon and as such they prepared.

Grimold did not sit idle reviewing ledgers. The curse of the lich and its malevolent touch was still woven into the fabric of the land and Grimold would have no more of it. Grimold would seek the aid of the Morrian clergy to see to the end of this spectral threat no doubt a vestige of with the aid of faith so as to complete Vortigern’s previous work. For every forty four days since the lich cursed the land specters would appear in the city and terrorize any who lingered in the streets as the moon rose until dawn. The newly established Dusk Watch would evolve from the usual nightly patrols and ensure no specter would roam free under the moonlight. Many nights, the knights of the Dusk Watch would descend into the shadowy catacombs beneath the land, searching for those who had vanished under the cover of darkness. Their efforts were not in vain, for with each journey, they uncovered more than just lost souls and allowed the morrian faithful deeper into the catacombs beneath. Whispers of kidnappings echoed through the damp corridors, and in the deepest recesses, the foul presence of ghouls lurked. The Garden of Morr was expanded beyond its old bounds, its walls rebuilt and its paths widened. Morrian iconography began to appear throughout Sontrailles, carved skulls set above gates and archways to ward off specters, ravens worked into stone lintels and banners, and iron grave-marks raised at crossroads where the veil was believed thinnest. Outside of the city the Knights Forlorn were reestablished and charged with assaulting the northern Geistunmund hills and extinguishing the undead threat. Volunteer companies joined them and in due time the territorial gains made by Vortigern were restored.

Within four years, Sontrailles had begun to resemble the city it had been before the coming of the Maggot Lord, though the memory of ruin had not yet faded. Merchants once more crowded the markets with wares drawn from neighboring lands. The clangor of forges rang through the streets from dawn until dusk, as blacksmiths and artisans labored to restore what had been broken, and farms were restored. Though the spirit of the people had not been broken, the shadow of another invasion and the constant threat of orks and worse left them grim and unsmiling, waiting for the hammer to fall at any moment. Grimold’s wife, Adelais, worked tirelessly to counter this as any good woman would, draping the city in color. Banners and long runners were raised atop rooftops and along the walls, snapping in the wind above the streets. She encouraged splendid attire among the nobility and made modest finery available to the common folk, until Sontrailles itself became a living kaleidoscope. While Grimold labored to harden the city for the wars yet to come, Adelais hardened the people in her own way, teaching them to live loudly beneath the doom’s shadow. So had hope returned to Sontrailles.

 In 2517 when the Northern Border Confederacy wished to wage war against Averland over control of tolls from Black Fire Pass, Grimold would not join Sontrailles to their cause, much to the ire of the princes. Instead he focused his efforts within his realm and continued bolstering its defenses against any future invasions and expanding settlements within his territories. In vexing irony, messengers would arrive after the battle at Grenzstadt, informing him his son Armand had saved Lord Durant of Akendorf by cutting down half a dozen greatswords, four of the Order of Sigmar’s Blood and then duelling the Elector Count Marius Leitdorf. The song of the “Wayfaring knight” and his great deeds at Grenzstadt along with his companions spread through the land written by a man of low renown, Francois. Sontrailles collectively sighed in relief when Averland did not retaliate after their victory, rather allowing the beaten border princes to flee with their tails between their legs after paying restitution. Grimold alone found no comfort in the outcome and he attempted to contain the spread of this song within his lands to little effect.

entries.title: Storm of Chaos
entries.body:
In 2520 when Waaagh! Ironjaw rampaged towards Black Fire Pass culminating into its Third battle, Sontrailles would repulse a small army of greenskins, overwhelming them with cannonfire and arrows forcing them to flee from the walls to be run down by knights and war wagons. In 2521 when the Storm of Chaos began and many more orc tribes attacked the Badlands, Sontrailles would commit less than a fourth of its forces to fight alongside the Northern Border Confederacy and the dwarfs of the Black Mountains to defend their lands in a series of battles while the rest defended their home though no attack came. Grimold relied on the speed of their wagons and lances once more, using a nearly all cavalry force to harry the orcs before committing to a thunderous charge that broke the greenskin lines.

The orc hordes were broken within four months and retreated back to the Badlands to be harried by the allied forces or face Settra’s wrath further south. A relief force was too late to assist Miragliano before its fall in 2522. After the storm was broken more orks came from the south and were met by the Sontrallais in full force.

entries.title: Trade Relations with Araby
entries.body:
For near a decade after the Storm of Chaos the Border Princes would have relative peace. Trade routes to Wissenland, Averland, and the west towards Bretonnia, Estalia, and Tilea were further established, increasing the flow of imports and exports flooding Sontrailles. The most unusual source of goods came when two Arabic ships were seen on the coasts and unloaded their cargo. Much to the surprise of the merchant guilds and indeed the Marquis himself the cargo of both ships were brought to the city with Armand and his companions at the head of the caravan and behind them envoys of the land of Al-Sahrun.

 Years ago Mathelin Belgard and his merchant company joined Armand’s questing party and travelled through the Badlands to Araby. By luck they would find their way to Al-Sahrun and build a bond with its people through warfare against a distant vampire bloodline in Araby and so the young Sultan Kamil ibn Sadri swore brotherhood with Armand. Thus a treaty of alliance and trade was secured and an embassy would be established in Sontrailles. This was a boon for Sontrailles, for now exotic goods too flowed through its gates and made its merchants and with them its people wealthy and with it more advanced blackpowder weaponry and culture. The Arabyan state of Al-Sahrun would remain the strongest ally of Sontrailles.

entries.title: Duel of the Two Vows
entries.body:
With this unprecedented peace in Grimold’s life, he began looking north after many years. The Divide where the Knights Forlorn held against the cyclical waves of undead stood strong, yet his mind began wandering towards total conquest of the northern hills as two of his predecessors did in days past. Much like them he prepared for a campaign, managing food stores, preparing arms and armor. Murmurs from nobles could be heard at court however. Many believed this was yet another ploy to usurp the place of the Lady with Morrian worship. Prodigious changes such as these reshaped the political and religious life of Sontrailles with a swiftness uncommon in settled realms, and those who lived through them had little leisure to weigh their meaning before they had already taken root. At first it appeared to be only a few rabble rousers, then many among the old nobility voiced their displeasure openly, and more did so in private. They lamented the sanctioning of gunpowder weapons, claiming that blackpowder weaponry had no place on fields of the glorious field of battle, and warning that such use of arms was what brought their neighbors to their dishonorable state and their unease at the elevation of Morr over the Lady of the Lake was the second spear in their political assault. Though her shrines were not stricken, many nobles feared that the patronage of King Death marked a turning away from chivalric virtue toward a colder, more macabre order. Hourglasses, skulls, and raven iconography were being chiseled into the newly repaired walls. They linked this, whether there is any truth to this or not, to Grimold's assent to allow peasants of means to purchase the rights of tenant farming which was received with particular bitterness, for it was argued it weakened the hierarchy imposed by the Lady, that these institutions were sacred and most necessary for society. The clergy of Morr answered such objections with dour certainty, that invasion and death were not matters of if but when, and bringing the realm to King Death’s order could Sontrailles hope to endure.

Debate raged for weeks after the reforms were enacted and the public announcement of the northern campaign made, giving both advocates and detractors fresh ammunition to rally their arguments. As the arguments intensified however, Marquise Adelais fell deathly ill and in the coming weeks no physician in the realm proved capable of bringing her to strength. It was clear her end was near and riders were sent to the Black Mountains in the north where Armand was sighted not a week prior. Meanwhile Grimold took her decline poorly. Sleepless nights reddened his eyes and the servants muttered that he did not touch his meals and a pall was cast over the court. It would be then when word came from the east that a host of warriors had began attacking the eastern border. A lightning campaign was conducted and the banners of old Bretonnian and Sontrallais heraldry was seen among the knights of the invading force. Initially, only a handful of towns and lesser hamlets were taken, and the incursions were believed by some to be little more than a passing raid. This belief was soon dispelled however and messengers arrived in haste from Baron Galchelin, bearing word that the enemy host was far greater than he or his vassals could reasonably withstand. Having gathered what men he might and found them insufficient for the defence of the frontier, the Baron sent formal petition unto the Marquis, beseeching immediate aid. Marquis Grimold, despite the condition in which he then found himself, did not dawdle upon receiving the Baron’s petition, yet the mustering of a host sufficient for the defense could not be accomplished in haste, for banners had first to be summoned and provisions gathered.

He therefore dispatched Armand, who had lately returned to Sontrailles to pay his respects at his mother’s grave, together with his companions, to the succour of Baron Galchelin. Messengers rode before them along every road, bearing orders that such knights, serjeants, and men-at-arms as could be gathered without delay were to join Armand upon the march. Thus, while the greater host of the Marquis was yet assembling, a smaller force was sent eastward with all possible speed to bolster the Baron’s defence and contest the enemy’s advance. Before joining Baron Galchelin, Armand divided part of his strength and sent two lesser forces ahead under the command of his close companions, Bernajoux de Gremes and Alain de Chatlon. Their charge was to ride swiftly through the threatened country and give aid to towns and villages that the Baron’s own men could not. The decision was undertaken at some risk, for Armand’s host was already but hastily assembled, yet the speed of the enemy’s advance left several settlements in danger of being overcome before the main force could come to their relief.

By the time Armand had joined his strength with that of Baron Galchelin near Lacan’s Ford, word had arrived concerning both detachments. Bernajoux had reached the town of Dimont shortly before it was overrun and there gave battle to the attacking company. According to the later accounts, he rode forth and met its captain in single combat, slew him, and put the remaining enemy to flight, thereby preserving the town from capture.

The news concerning Alain however brought sorrow. While advancing through the eastern country, he was challenged to single combat by the leader of an opposing company and accepted. In the duel that followed, Alain was slain. His body was sent bearing his arms and armor.

Battle of Lacan’s Ford

The battle was recorded by the bard Francois and presented as thus:

“The first great meeting of arms befell at Lacan’s Ford, where Armand, with such strength as he had gathered in haste, came against the foremost companies of the returning host. Baron Galchelin had aforetime drawn sundry of his scattered men unto the crossing, deeming that place more meet for defence than the open country farther east. Armand came thither but shortly before the enemy and there took command of the Baron’s household men, the serjeants of the country, and such knights as had answered the summons upon his march. The old accounts make much of the disorder of that first gathering, for the companies came severally and by divers roads, many weary from hard riding and few knowing the true number or purpose of those who came against them.

Battle was joined when the foreign host sought to win the ford by force of arms. Their first charges fell sorely upon Galchelin’s foremost companies and thrust several from their ground, yet the narrowness of the crossing profited the attackers little, for they could not bring the whole weight of their host to bear. Armand therefore bade the foot stand fast upon the approaches, whilst war wagons were drawn forth and men bearing bows, crossbows, and shot were set amongst them to strengthen the line. This manner of war gave great offence unto many of the enemy chivalry, who afterward charged the Sontrallais with having forsaken the old usages of honorable battle. Yet wrath availed them naught. Time and again they assailed the crossing, and time and again were they cast back. When the day grew late, the foreign host withdrew beyond ready pursuit, and so was the field reckoned unto Sontrailles, though neither side had suffered such grievous hurt as might decide the war.

Only after the fighting was ended was the true nature of the enemy made plain. Among the knights taken alive were men bearing the arms and devices of old Bretonnian and Sontrallais houses, and under questioning they named themselves the sons of those who had departed the realm in years long past. They denied that they had come as conquerors, but called themselves restorers, saying that Sontrailles had wandered from the ordinances of the Lady through the waxing worship of Morr, the sufferance of blackpowder arms, and the new laws ordained beneath Marquis Grimold. Word of these sayings passed swiftly from hall to hall amongst the lords of the east, and that which had first been taken for no more than a great raid upon the marches was thereafter understood as a quarrel touching not only land and lordship, but the very faith, custom, and right ordering of the realm.”

Carnage and Loyalty

While the eastern campaign continued, Marquis Grimold pressed ahead with the general muster of the realm. The response, however, revealed the depth of the religious and political divisions that had developed during the preceding reforms. A number of lords who remained closely attached to the cult of the Lady either failed to answer the summons or contributed forces significantly smaller than their obligations and resources would ordinarily have permitted. Most avoided outright defiance, instead citing poor harvests, local security, sickness, delayed levies, or other practical impediments. Contemporary chroniclers were nevertheless inclined to interpret such excuses as deliberate hesitation.

This reluctance caused considerable concern among the Marquis’s more reliable supporters. The fear was not merely that Grimold lacked troops, but that a substantial portion of the nobility appeared to be withholding judgment until the course of the war became clearer. Lords sympathetic to Morr increasingly regarded such conduct as evidence of disloyalty, while adherents of the Lady argued that the conflict concerned matters of faith and tradition too grave to be treated as an ordinary feudal summons. As a result, the size of each contingent sent to the Marquis became politically significant, and even otherwise routine delays in mustering were closely scrutinized.

The conduct of Grimold and Armand consequently assumed unusual importance. Supporters of the Morrian reforms looked to their victories as proof that the new military and religious order of Sontrailles remained viable, citing that Armand himself had been blessed by King Death personally, flying with Ravens Wings. Meanwhile many nobles of the older Bretonnian tradition watched for signs that the ruling house had abandoned the chivalric ideals from which its authority had historically been derived. The campaign therefore became, in the eyes of later historians, not only a military contest but a broader test of legitimacy. The allegiance of several undecided houses remained conditional, and both factions understood that success in the field might determine the religious and political character of the realm for generations.

After hearing these reports and those from the field Grimold, against the advice of his council, would not send his personal knights and the marshal to assist Armand, rather ordered that they must march with him when the army was mustered. He ascertained that Armand needed to take command in person and thereby prove his worth before the people, and any success won beneath the direction of more senior commanders would lessen his image as his standing among the lords of the land would most likely depend on how he acquitted himself of war. He could not rely on bardic tales from far off wars.

Clash upon the Violet Fields

The next large scale battle came upon the Violet Fields so named for the purple colored grasses that covered that country in the colder months. By then Armand had been joined by further companies of knights, serjeants, men-at-arms, and several war wagons sent from the neighboring lordships. The returning host likewise had gathered strength, and for the first time both armies were drawn up in such number that neither could easily withdraw without giving the other advantage. The foreign knights placed their chief hope in a great mounted assault, trusting that the weight of their chivalry would break the Sontrallais line before the foot could properly stand against them.

Their first charge fell with great violence and scattered several lesser companies upon Armand’s left, while a number of Sontrallais knights were driven from the field. Yet Armand had caused wagons, stakes, and companies of foot to be set where the ground narrowed between two low ridges, and thither the enemy were drawn. There they came under bowshot and blackpowder fire before meeting the spears and bills of the waiting infantry who through great cost held their ground. When the enemy charge had spent itself, Armand ordered his remaining cavalry forward, and the fighting became confused and bitter, knight meeting knight beneath banners bearing devices that had once stood upon the same side.By evening the Restorers of the Grail yielded the field and withdrew eastward in good order, leaving many dead among the violet grasses. The victory was counted greater than that at Lacan’s Ford, though it was dearly bought, and was not decisive.

The Duel of the Two Vows

The battle remembered as the Duel of the Two Vows was the last battle of the war. By that time the Restorers of the Grail had gathered beneath the command of Gylbarde de Barrault, once upon a time the greatest knight errant of Armand’s own generation and once his sworn brother. In the years since his departure from Sontrailles, Gylbarde had completed the Grail Quest and returned as a Grail Knight of considerable renown. His presence lent great weight to the cause of the restorationists, for among the adherents of the Lady he was taken as living proof that their undertaking enjoyed divine favor and with him three other grail knights. Armand in his own journey had become one of the foremost champions of King Death in the eyes of the common man. Thus, when the two armies met upon the field, both believed it was a contest between two visions of the realm represented by men who had once been brothers.

The battle itself was bitterly fought, neither side gaining a decisive advantage in its opening hours. The knights of the grail repeatedly pressed the Sontrallais center, while Armand’s infantry and household cavalry held their ground under considerable strain. It was during this fighting that Gylbarde rode forth and challenged Armand openly and thus the duel of which the battle was named began. Accounts differ as to whether the challenge had been arranged beforehand or arose amidst the battle, though all agree that the surrounding knights drew back sufficiently to permit the two men to meet. Their combat was afterward much embellished by poets, but even the more restrained chronicles describe it as prolonged and severe. Gylbarde fought bellowing the vows of the Lady and the Grail, while Armand bore the symbols of Morr and wielded Nightbrandt in the service of what his followers called King Death.

The duel ended after minutes of fighting. Gylbarde was ultimately overcome, though whether slain outright or mortally wounded was disputed. Some say he was given one final chance to surrender and enter the grace of the Marquis. Others say he was mercilessly slaughtered. His fall broke the spirit of the restorationists, while the Sontrallais, seeing their commander still standing with weapon raised in the air, renewed their assault and drove the enemy from the field.

After the battle his wound festered and fever followed. The physicians treated the wound but his condition worsened and day by day his strength left him until he could no longer walk upright without assistance and still refused to stop personally holding court, propped upright on his throne.

Within days Grimold de Mousillon would succumb, for no physician nor priestess of Shallya could cure him. Armand would take his rightful place on the throne after matters were discussed.

entries.title: War Against the Night and Reign of Armand, 1560
entries.body:
“..Today justice was done so that all might see the fate of those who worship the night. King Death has seen fit to grant me Raven’s Wings, and no villain can escape his hand..”

- Armand de Sontrailles, as recorded by the bard Francois, Winter 1560 (2538 IC)

 Preparations for war were made quickly, for the new Marquis made clear his intentions: the Northern Geistenmund hills would be taken and all who lived under the thrall of the night in the region would be freed. Fortuitously for the new lord his predecessor had begun many months prior. The food stores were filled and provisions for the campaigning armies were prepared. Among the warband of Armand were experienced vampire hunters who had studied their foe for a lifetime. They would be dispersed into the armies to advise the war leaders and fight vampires. Most of Sontraille's forces were brought for the northern campaign to take the hills while he sent v Guion le Brave and Bernajoux de Gremes with an army west to liberate towns rumored to be ruled by vampire lords.

Over the following weeks, Armand’s forces engaged in a series of battles. Hordes of undead descended to the valley as necromancers stirred in the hills. Yet time and again the Sontrallais host held firm. As the army pressed deeper into the hills, Armand split his forces to sweep the ridges systematically. Skirmishes erupted along narrow passes, where the undead tried to overwhelm the knights with sheer numbers. Siege engines and war wagons pummeled the enemy from afar, while squads of hunters tracked vampire lieutenants and dispatched them with precision. By the campaign’s end, the northern Geistenmund Hills were wrested from darkness, the necromantic influence purged from key passes, and the ridges fortified for Sontrailles’ occupation. Even as total domination of the valley and northern hills neared Armand knew the battle was not won. In the west villages were liberated and word from the surviving villagers told of Sonnental, the bastion where the vampiric aristocracy hid.

 In the last days of the conquest preparations for an assault on Sonnental began. Bernajoux and Guion’s forces raided the towns surrounding Sonnental and liberated them, then began slowly surrounding the town. By the time the main army arrived siege lines were dug. By day, the engines of Sontrailles hurled stone against its battlements. By night, the defenders answered in kind. The gates would creak open without warning, and armored riders would sally forth, in a fury their blades cutting through the unwary before vanishing again behind the gates. It was the third day that a breach was made along the eastern curtain wall. Armand ordered the assault at dawn. By mid morning the keep was secured and the bodies of the vampire lords were dragged into the courtyard, staked, and set aflame before the assembled host. The pyres burned long and foul, and many turned their faces from the smoke. When at last the flames died and nothing remained but ash, it was declared that Sonnental was cleansed. Thus ended the dominion of the night over that city, and the banners of Sontrailles were raised above its walls.

 Subsequent to this victory Armand would found the High Chivalric Order of the Shroud and dedicate it to “King Death” as Morr would become widely known in the realm. Their seat would be built on the opposite side of Sontrailles of Aedric’s Rest and known as the Keep of Deserved Rest. Along with them the Synod of the Raven’s Messengers, a cult of Morr, would be officially recognized as King Death’s cult within the realm. The Cult of the Lady would not stand idle within the city however, and many who remained dedicated to her would form the High Chivalric Order of the Silver Lilies and would use Aedric’s Rest as their keep and Godefroy de Cervellier as their Grandmaster.

 Trade with Al-Sahrun would bring about changes in the realm. Besides bringing vast wealth it also brought techniques known to Araby to the Sontrallais. Arabyan alchemical techniques would be used to improve facets of life, including improving the process by which the alloy used in Virtuous Steel was made and thus enhancing the final product. Blackpowder weapons would become far more accurate and the range improved as well and as a direct consequence far more common. Large cannons were replacing ballistas atop the walls, smaller culverins were mounted upon the war wagons and an increasing number of serjeants outfitted their retinues with handguns. It would come to a head when Armand removed the restrictions on the use of blackpowder weaponry. The ensuing political battles among the nobles bled into the two knightly orders, leading to fights in the streets between them. While bloody they would almost always cease once one grouped yield and rarely to the death. These forced more immediate resolutions in the discussions of not long term solutions.

entries.title: Crusades into Sylvania
entries.body:
The Marquis’ hatred of vampirekind and all of their ilk was common knowledge among the people and so when Abbot Geistwäch of Siegfriedhof appealed for aid it was only natural for him to marshal a force bound for Sylvania itself. While there were no words spoken against the cause of the crusade, there was dissent for the expenditure for the campaign. While Sontrailles had been known for their gaudy colors and baroque armor in the theater of war, some would murmur that Armand was becoming the Marquis of “Self-Magnification” who led a crusade of “opulent display” due to rich furnishings purchased for the journey. Among these considered egregious, would be three thousand green satin tents, one thousand velvet horse blankets, black satin tents for each Grave Warden priest, purple dyed silken tents for the magicians, and for his personal corps, blankets of silk interwoven with gold. The journey itself would take the army through Averland which required negotiations with its government. It was not forgotten that the wayfaring knight and his companions had slain knights of their orders but most vexing was the attempt on the elector count’s life, which was not forgotten in the intervening years. Correspondence with the noble Alptraum family would secure the safety of the army to journey unmolested towards Sylvania, most likely a show of power and one-upmanship to the Leitdorf family for a small price.

The journey itself to Siegfriedhof was relatively uneventful, minor battles in the Black Fire Pass and Stirland left the army intact for the battles ahead. In Siegfriedhof they joined the Knights of the Raven and Stirlander forces in battle against the forces of the vampire counts, driving them towards Hunger Wood where they faced the vampire lord Ottmar Von Carstein. The thick foliage made it difficult for regiments to keep ranks and thus the crusaders were split from one another soon after the fighting began. Such was the chaos that many of the Knights of the Raven and local militia fell back while Stirlander state troops held ground. It would take time for the crusaders to regain order within their ranks though the night would be won with the vampire lord’s head taken. It would be written by chroniclers that

“ As the Siegfriedhofers of meager heart fled, Sir Regnault’s throat was pierced by the black runed blade of Ottmar Von Carstein. With a righteous rage from his sword-brother’s death, Bernajoux de Grèmes wielded Wind’s Roar with speed and strength unmatched and thus hewed the dark lord in twain and his blood knights with him.”

The crusade would continue for five months, pushing ever deeper into Sylvania until the supply lines were stretched too thin. With their footholds gained the crusaders would return back to Siegfriedhof and then Sontrailles. This would be one of four yearly crusades into Sylvania before matters in the region of Sontrailles forced the Marquis to postpone his plans, though years later he would continue his vision of eradicating the vampire menace from the fallen land.Through these campaigns, friendship was cultivated between the Marquis and the noble House of Alptraum. Their cooperation would mature into a binding treaty of trade bringing goods and wealth to both.

entries.title: War in the Depths
entries.body:
During the crusades expansion into the underground catacombs would lead to mines being established and exits from the city out into the surrounding hills and valleys being constructed. These tunnels from the city would bring them deeper than previous eras and with it conflict with the denizens of the deep. Risen dead from eras past were a common danger to the miners as they tunneled deeper and disturbed their tombs. Other subterranean menaces made themselves known when the miners came upon tunnels not of their making. Vicious ratmen attacked them in the dark tunnels quickly. Weeks would go by as groups of miners disappeared until a singular survivor escaped to the surface to warn his superiors, the skaven were attacking.

 As quickly as the citizens on the surface were warned the ratmen tunneled their way up and began their assault, earlier than planned. Great burrows erupted around the city at first then within, splitting streets as the skaven poured forth. Clan Vordrit made itself known as its Warlord Skeepus rose from the depths upon his massive gromril plated bonecrusher, his vengeance had been years in the making.

Even as the burrows split the streets and the vermin host poured forth in shrieking tumult, the alarm bells rang from tower to tower. Steel answered claw. The garrison rallied beneath their banners, and the knights of the orders formed ranks where the earth had sundered. Warlord Skeepus drove his Bonecrusher through the outer wards, breaking barricades and scattering militia as chaff before his blade. Yet for all his fury, the defenders yielded ground with discipline rather than rout. Streets were abandoned only to become killing lanes. Oil was cast, bridges collapsed, and whole quarters denied to the foe by planned conflagration. The ratmen found themselves ensnared in a desperate close battle where their numbers strangled their own advance. At last the Marquis himself took the field upon his winged mount, and the counterstroke was delivered. Knights thundered through the smoke filled streets, crashing into the heart of Clan Vordrit’s mass. Historian Michault wrote of his account of the battle :

“ King Death’s Right Hand crashed down upon the daemon rat like a thunderbolt from the heavens and swung Nightbrandt in a wide arc and its blade bit deep and rent the beast’s armor. And thus the tide was turned and the noble knights drove back the fiends squealing back to their dwellings below.”

Denied surprise and beset from every side, the skaven faltered. Their warlord, grievously wounded, gave the shrill order to withdraw. As swiftly as they had risen, so too did they vanish, retreating into their tunnels dragging their prisoners, leaving their dead and wounded as they escaped into the dark. Afterward many men were sent into the burrows seeking those who had been taken, and some few were brought forth alive. Yet of many others no tidings were ever had, and it was held that they had perished in the deeps. This would not be the last of Skweepus the Chainlord.’

From this the Depth’s Watch was established. They were charged with patrolling the tunnels under Sontrailles and other mines in the region to protect the good people from the vile predations of the fiendish ratmen.

entries.title: Arabyan Wars
entries.body:
The covenant between Sontrailles and Al-Sahrun was no mere mercantile convenience. Trade enriched both realms with merchant ships travelling to and from both realms across the Southern Sea even against the High Elves of Ulthuan’s decrees yet both realms stood amidst potential enemies in these dark times. Armand de Sontrailles would ride to the aid of Sultan Kamil ibn Sadri when a rival power threatened their borders and he appealed for aid. When the courier arrived at the court of Armand he began at once hiring ships to transport nearly ten thousand troops across the sea to aid his ally. By the time they arrived Al-Sahrun was nearly overrun, the forces of Doukesh and Al-Jawri had begun annexing Al-Sahrun’s lands. By no small effort the Sontrallais and Sahruni warriors were able to push back the invader for it took months of grinding successive engagements across the land to retake the cities of Al-Sahrun.

At the First Battle of Qasr al-Nimr, the banners of Sontrailles were seen beside the yellow and white standards of Sultan Kamil ibn Sadri. Armand de Sontrailles himself is said to have taken the center, anchoring the line with his heavily armored foot knights and cavalry while Sahruni cavalry harried the flanks with their cavalry rifles. The forces of Doukesh, overconfident from their rapid advances, committed heavily against the allied center and were met with disciplined volleys of jezzails and a thunderous counter charge by the knights and kontoi supported by magic. The battle halted the enemy’s momentum and secured the road to the outer settlements. It is said by chroniclers who witnessed the battle:

“ As the Sahruni and Sontrallais knights charged with great courage in their hearts, Estelle, Magestrix of Sontrailles, weaved magics from the breath of her familiars and cast great spells to the woe of Doukesh and Al-Jawri.”

After Qasr al-Nimr, at Wadi Safur, Sahruni riders lured the men of Al-Jawri into narrow ground where Sontraillais infantry held firm behind great siege towers. Five times the invaders attempted to break the line, five times they were repelled. It is noted that supply proved invaluable as Armand’s fleet ensured the allied host did not wither. The most decisive engagement came before the walls of Taghreb, whose fall would have split Al-Sahrun in twain. There the allied host fought from dawn until the stars were visible, driving back successive assaults and finally turning defense into pursuit. When Armand ordered the advance at dusk, the combined cavalry of Sontrailles and Al-Sahrun broke the enemy’s cohesion.

By the campaign’s end, the forces of Doukesh and Al-Jawri were driven beyond the disputed marches and compelled to sue for terms and ceded much land to Sultan Kamil. From this eight month campaign the bonds of Sontrailles and Al-Sahrun strengthened and the Sahruni would sail the Southern Sea and aid Sontrailles many times.

entries.title: At Present
entries.body:
The reign of Armand de Sontrailles has been characterized by his crusades and preparation for the Second Son of the Great Kurgan even as Tamurkhan’s invasion was more than fifty years ago. The outer walls of the city were heightened and thickened, their towers refashioned to command overlapping fields of fire with presighted ranges. Beneath them ran new sally ports and galleries, so that men might move unseen and strike where least expected. A lower enceinte was raised before the greater wall,for should its gates be forced, the foe would find himself confined between two rings of stone, exposed to missile fire from above. The districts were segregated and prepared such that each street could be turned into a killing lane with ease by barricade points and strong houses at crossings. Buildings closest to the walls have tunnels beneath so that if the chance arises, defenders can appear behind invading forces to flank them and turn a street cannon upon them to deadly effect. Each district would be a fortress on its own.

The continuing advances of blackpowder weaponry is still a subject that the nobility raises their noses at, however it is becoming more common among the commoners as the decades go by. These weapons are brought to the crusades of the restless ruler, fighting orks, vampires, skaven, and any perceived threat to Sontrailles most campaign seasons. These weapons too are further improved by the magics established by Magestrix Estelle who by her apprentices is able to weave runes of shyish into ammunition.

Her school of magic has less than forty students, taught in the ways of the Amethyst order that she once learned with Arabyan tradition infused and they aid in the wars of Sontrailles as well as its daily life, strengthening defensive runes, maintaining leylines, and other matters. Runecrafting has become its own art, such that the Durocher family has incorporated it within their tradition of smithing.

With this era of stability comes those who would seek change. Many times the council brings up the possibility of severing all ties to Bretonnia and crowning Armand as King of Sontrailles and its lands. So far the Marquis has waved away these comments, speaking of the commission granted from the Royarch himself over a century ago, however his wife Lisette has hinted of plans unspoken.

entries.title: Notable Settlements
entries.body:
Charfourrier

 The town of Charfourrier is ruled by Baron René de Charfourrier, a member of the inner circle of the High Chivalric Order of the Shroud. Situated southeast of the southern Geistenmund Hills, Charfourrier is a fortified settlement of nearly three thousand souls, with a further five thousand dispersed among the villages, hamlets, and farmsteads of the surrounding countryside.

The lands about Charfourrier are among the most fertile in Sontrailles and are commonly described as the breadbasket of the realm. Beyond the town walls, cultivated fields stretch across the countryside in great patchworks, broken only by villages, pasturelands, and the estates of the local nobility. Grain constitutes the principal harvest, though the abundant grazing lands likewise support considerable herds of cattle, sheep, and horses.
