Noble landlords oversee broad estates worked by tenant farmers and serfs, ensuring that each season's harvest is gathered and stored while maintaining stout watchtowers from which approaching raiders may be sighted.If the knights and their men at arms are not close enough to protect their charges with speed, the millers are known to be well armed and brutal.

Produce from the surrounding estates is carried by cart into Charfourrier and its dependent villages, where grain is milled, livestock traded, and stores collected for distribution. What is not required for local consumption is subsequently dispatched throughout Sontrailles, making the town an important supplier of food to less fertile districts and to the larger cities of the realm. The fortunes of the Baron and much of the local nobility are consequently tied closely to the success of the harvest. Baron René is known to spend a considerable portion of this wealth upon the equipment and maintenance of his serjeants and soldiers rather than upon lavish additions to his household.

The military traditions of Charfourrier similarly reflect the character of its countryside. Its forces consist primarily of infantry and cavalry, with comparatively little emphasis placed upon blackpowder troops. Trained artillerists are rarer still, and the employment of large engines such as trebuchets is uncommon among its contingents. Instead, Charfourrier has developed considerable proficiency in the use of war wagons, which accompany its mounted forces and provide mobile strongpoints from which infantry may secure roads, crossings, and the flanks of cavalry formations.

The people of Charfourrier are widely regarded as orderly, disciplined, and unusually attentive to time. Punctuality is considered a mark of good character, while tardiness is treated with considerably less tolerance than elsewhere in the realm. Local custom holds that a man who cannot arrive when he has promised cannot readily be trusted and excuses for lateness, whatever the circumstance, are seldom received with much sympathy.

Coutenagne

Coutenagne is well known for its wines such that the locals dare say it is the best wine in the region, and of course, the Old World. Count Perrin de Coutenagne is well known to be persnickety, going about managing his holdings personally, spending much time in the saddle rounding the area surrounded by his retinue. While its vineyards are the envy of many it is its textile mills and dye makers that earn the baron a hefty sum. Old wive’s tales tell of the flavor of the wine coming from the blood soaked land, the earth having supposedly taken on some part of that sanguine character. Such stories are generally dismissed by vintners, though they have done little harm to the reputation or sale of the local vintage . Because of the availability of good quality wine and are rather renowned for their love of drink in stark contrast to laws prohibiting public intoxication. Coutenagne is also notable for producing an unusually large number of Sontrailles’ poets, lyricists, and wandering versifiers. Local tradition attributes this to the beauty of the countryside, whose vineyards, rolling pasture, and wooded hills are said to stir the poetic soul. Less charitable observers insist that the abundance of wine is the more likely explanation, such that the reputation of its people is of drunken sloths. Beyond the vineyards, much of the surrounding pastoral land is devoted to the raising of sheep and horses. Sheep provide the wool necessary for the local textile industry, while horse breeding has developed into a profitable trade and a local tradition of horse rearing has arisen.

Of its nearly three thousand inhabitants, almost fifteen percent serve as professional soldiers, an unusually high proportion for a settlement of its size. This is owed in large part to Baron Rochfort de Coutenagne, who is habitually among the first of the Marquis’s vassals to pledge troops whenever called upon. Some hold that this eagerness is less of martial enthusiasm than of a desire to remain in the Marquis’s favor. Such suspicions are bolstered by the fact that Rochfort has, on more than one occasion, been offered the opportunity to discharge part of his military obligation through scutage, only to refuse and provide more soldiers in person instead.

Roucourt

 A great city set among the surrounding hills, it serves foremost as a fortified center for the protection and administration of the region’s numerous mines, from which ores of considerable quality are extracted. Much of the common population finds employment either in the mines themselves or in the smithies and foundries of the city, while a substantial number make their living transporting ore from the workings to the furnaces and workshops where it is smelted and wrought.

On the outskirts of the city stands the manor of House Durocher, together with the family’s extensive forges. It is here that the Durochers produce weapons and armor of Virtuous Steel for the knights and nobility of Sontrailles, employing a closely guarded process that has long been one of the family’s most valuable possessions. The Durocher estate is considerable enough to resemble a small settlement in its own right, containing workshops, storehouses, servants’ quarters, and barracks, as well as a permanent garrison of household knights, serjeants, and musketeers sworn directly to the family. The city is likewise noted for its jewelers and lapidaries, many of whom work by commission for noble households throughout the realm. Because of their proximity to the mines, these craftsmen are often afforded first choice among newly recovered gemstones before the remainder are sold or transported elsewhere, granting the city’s workshops access to particularly fine materials. The Blacksmiths’ Guild also maintains one of its principal halls within the city. There, aspiring smiths who gain admission may apprentice beneath recognized masters of the craft and receive instruction in the forging of weapons, armor, tools, and other worked goods. The guildhall itself is a broad, square-built structure containing workshops, offices, storerooms, and meeting chambers, and is rarely quiet during the working day, with guilders, apprentices, merchants, and factors continually fussing about

Among the towns the soldiers of Baron Raulin de Roucourt have taken to blackpowder weapons the quickest. Cannons and other siege equipment are manufactured in his workshops and as such artillerymen are drilled night and day. Little agriculture can be achieved in the rugged hills of Roucourt and as such they rely on its neighbors and shepherds for foodstuffs. The Depth Watch have a strong base in the area, for many squads delve deep into the mines to ensure safety from hazards and predators. While seemingly counterintuitive the game of golf is quite popular in the hilly region.

Flumontel

At the mouth of the River Trebleca stands the bustling city of Flumontel, a settlement of some eight thousand souls and the principal seaport of the realm. The present city was raised upon the ruins of old Somjek, its growth financed in no small part by the celebrated voyage of Mathelin Belgard to Araby many years ago. Belgard returned with his ships laden with treasure and costly goods, much of that wealth subsequently being invested in the rebuilding of the harbor, warehouses, quays, and defenses. From these beginnings Flumontel developed into the foremost maritime center of Sontrailles.

A sizeable Arabyan community occupies a quarter of its own within the city. There, with the permission of Count Aubert, a temple dedicated to their Nehekharan gods was permitted to be established. Officially, the concession was intended to encourage closer relations with the princes and merchant lords of Araby; less charitable observers have long suggested that the Count was equally interested in the customs duties and commercial privileges such friendship might bring him. The markets of Flumontel bear more resemblance to the bazaars of distant Araby than to the market squares of inland Sontrailles. Imported spices, dyes, silks, glassware, perfumes, metals, and other foreign goods are unloaded upon the quays before being sold locally or placed upon carts and river craft bound for Sontrailles and the settlements beyond. Merchants from throughout the lands bordering the tempestuous Black Gulf may be encountered in its streets, and on busy days a dozen languages may be heard within little more than a single market square.

Among those inhabitants not of Bretonnian stock, Estalians, Tileans, and Arabyans form the largest communities. A much smaller number of Sea Elves have likewise settled there. By grant of the local lord, they possess a cordoned street of their own and generally remain apart from the other inhabitants. Whatever prestige their race might possess elsewhere, their quarter in Flumontel is a rather neglected place, its buildings cramped and weather worn and its lanes considerably poorer than those surrounding the principal markets.

Flumontel is also home to the greater part of the realm's navy. Its warships patrol the coast and approaches to the Trebleca, many mounting cannon of Arabyan manufacture or pattern. Consequently, the city's military obligations differ considerably from those of inland settlements. Rather than supplying large bodies of foot levies, Flumontel provides sailors, shipboard fighting men, marines, dockworkers, and other personnel necessary for maintaining the fleet. The first generations of its seamen were instructed in the arts of navigation and naval warfare by experienced Arabyan and Tilean sailors, whose methods left a lasting influence upon the city's maritime traditions. Commerce nevertheless remains the constant business of Flumontel. On an ordinary day, scores of vessels may be found lying at anchor or tied along its quays, their crews loading and unloading cargo before departing once again into the Black Gulf. Thus nearly every foreign luxury reaching Sontrailles passes through Flumontel at one time or another, and much of the wealth of the realm passes through the city in return.

As a port city, it is little wonder that Manaan is revered above all other gods, and even the Count himself is known to be a devoted adherent of the sea god’s cult. The worship of other deities is by no means absent, yet the people of Flumontel commonly hold that the authority of every other god ends where the sea begins. Beyond the harbor mouth, they say, all men sail beneath Manaan’s dominion.

Bacque

On the eastern border of Sontrailles is the town of Bacque, ruled by Count Andres de Bacque, one of the few lords of Estalian blood to hold land within the realms. Its position upon the frontier has given the town some military importance, though its prosperity rests primarily upon agriculture and animal husbandry.

The countryside surrounding Bacque is well suited to grazing, and much of the land is given over to the raising of sheep, goats, cattle, and other livestock. Dairy production forms an especially important part of the local economy, with goat's milk and cow's milk being sold throughout the surrounding settlements either fresh or made into butter, cheeses, and other preserved goods. Wool, hides, and livestock are likewise traded in considerable quantities.Though lacking the more specialized industries found in some of the larger towns of Sontrailles, Bacque is nevertheless one of the principal food producing settlements of the eastern region. Its farms and pastures supply not only the local population but also neighboring garrisons and communities whose own lands are less productive. Because of this, the fortunes of Bacque are closely tied to the health of its herds and the success of each year's harvest. Its strategic position upon the eastern frontier has compelled the maintenance of a strong military presence. Bacque keeps a sizeable garrison charged with watching the border, giving warning of incursions, and holding the town and its approaches until reinforcements can be summoned. The local soldiery is consequently accustomed to frequent musters, patrols, and prolonged periods of frontier duty, while the Count’s own household troops form the core around which the defenses of the town are organized.

Peculiarly, however, the household of Count Andres de Bacque differs greatly from those maintained by most lords of comparable station. Whereas such men ordinarily surround themselves with household knights and well-drilled serjeants, the most formidable element of the Count’s retinue consists of a band of Black Orcs accompanied by three giants. Their service began years prior in which during a waugh! where Count de Bacque slew their warboss Krokrog Bonecruncha in single combat and then imposed his will upon the surviving warriors by the only argument they were inclined to respect, superior violence. Rather than destroy the remainder of the band, he compelled them into his service, promising plentiful food, strong drink, and, above all, “a good fight” for the rest of their days. Though not disciplined by conventional standards, the Black Orcs and giants have proven brutally effective in battle and have become one of the more infamous features of Bacque’s frontier garrison.

While the Orcs generally remain confined to barracks well away from the inhabited settlements, the giants are a far more familiar sight throughout the county. They are regularly employed on patrols under the command of Sir Izan, whose presence is considered necessary both to direct them and to ensure that their considerable enthusiasm does not become troublesome to the inhabitants they are charged with protecting.

Of the three, the best known is a giant who took for himself the name Montes. He carries an enormous iron bell suspended from a heavy chain, which he sounds each night as the appointed hour of curfew approaches. The tolling can be heard for leagues across the surrounding countryside and has become a familiar part of life in Bacque. Villagers commonly reckon the closing of gates, shutters, and taverns by the distant ringing of Montes’s bell.

Brulivaux

 North of Sontrailles lies the town of Brulivaux, named for the flame colored grasses characteristic of the surrounding country. The settlement first grew around the site of the largest stronghold of the Knights of the Forlorn, where great furnaces were maintained for the burning of undead corpses recovered after battle. Though its origins were consequently rather grim, modern Brulivaux is renowned for the striking beauty of its countryside. From spring through autumn the surrounding grasses take on a brilliant flame red hue, fading with the onset of winter into a deep purple. More than six thousand souls now inhabit the town.

Brulivaux has earned particular distinction in the martial contests regularly organized by the lords of Sontrailles. Its companies have won more of the small wars than those of any other settlement in the region, and its levies are consequently regarded among the most disciplined and dependable in the realm. They are drilled with unusual frequency and are especially proficient in the employment of war wagons, being able to arrange them rapidly into defensive positions and break those formations with equal efficiency when ordered to resume the march. Their ability to employ the wagons in both static defense and mobile warfare is a considerable source of pride to Baron Gautier.

The town is also home to the Abbey of the Ravens, where aspiring Raven Messengers undertake the first stages of their instruction. It is likewise an important center for the training of mourners, who are taught the rites, customs, and practical duties expected of their profession before being dispatched throughout the realm.

Glassmaking forms another important part of the local economy. A nearby deposit of particularly fine quartz with a red hue provides the principal raw material for Brulivaux's glassworks, whose furnaces produce both common wares and finer pieces for export. The abundance of fuel and mineral resources has encouraged a concentration of skilled glassworkers and furnacemen within the town. The broad and relatively level country surrounding Brulivaux has also shaped its military culture. Artillery units have ample ground upon which to conduct live drills, maneuver guns, and practice the rapid establishment of firing positions. Regular exercises have consequently produced a disproportionate number of skilled artillerists, many of whom later enter the service of noble households or the Marquis's own forces.

Among the common people, thrown-ball is particularly popular. Although played throughout Sontrailles, the game enjoys an especially strong following in Brulivaux, where the open fields surrounding the town provide ample ground for both informal matches and organized contests.

Cervellier

Nestled in the heartlands of Sontrailles, Cervellier is home to more than seven thousand souls and is renowned throughout the realm for the quality of its horses. Generations of careful breeding have produced stock held in particularly high esteem, and great attention is given to the preservation of established bloodlines. Local scribes maintain meticulous records of pedigrees, coverings, births, and sales, allowing breeders to trace the ancestry of valuable animals across many generations and thereby safeguard both the purity and reputation of their lines.

Among the Sontraillais, the inhabitants of Cervellier are sometimes described as being “horse-mad.” It is commonly said that a Cervellier man's wife has good reason to be jealous of his horse. Jabs such as this are quite accurate in fact, for considerable sums are often spent upon the feeding, grooming, training, and equipment of favored mounts.

The countryside surrounding the city is dominated by broad and carefully maintained pastures, where stallions and mares graze beneath the supervision of herdsmen and experienced horse-masters. Breeding estates range from modest family holdings to extensive studs maintained by noble houses, and animals from Cervellier are purchased for purposes ranging from farm work and carriage pulling to hunting and war. The finest destriers and coursers command considerable prices and are sought after by knights throughout Sontrailles.

Beyond its equine trade, Cervellier possesses a modest but dependable agricultural economy. The surrounding farms produce grain, hay, oats, and other fodder in quantities sufficient not only for the human population but for the enormous number of horses maintained in the district. Smiths, farriers, saddlers, leatherworkers, and harness-makers likewise form an important portion of the town's craftsmen, supplying everything from common horseshoes and pack saddles to richly decorated tack and barding intended for noble warhorses.

Each year Cervellier hosts the celebrated Stallion's Run, traditionally the final great horse race of the Sontraillais year. Riders and spectators travel from across the realm to attend, and for the duration of the contest the town's population swells considerably. Beginning shortly after dawn and continuing until the sun sinks behind the surrounding hills, riders compete along a demanding course laid through open pasture, country roads, and the ridges overlooking the valley. The event tests not merely speed, but endurance, horsemanship, and the ability of both horse and rider to negotiate difficult ground.

Victory in the Stallion's Run carries considerable prestige, with successful riders commonly receiving purses of gold, finely worked tack, or costly barding in addition to the honor of the title. Grandmaster Godefroy de Cervellier famously claimed the race for four consecutive years, an achievement that appeared likely to stand unchallenged until he was finally unseated by Sir Crispin de Bouhier, whose victory remains one of the better-known upsets in the competition's history.

entries.title: Nobility
entries.body:
All landing owning nobles are knights, yet not all knights are land owning nobles. What this means in Sontrailles is that knighthood is the first step within nobility. It is a highly stratified system where land owning is vassalized often from higher ranking nobles to lower ranking ones, unless one were to take land on their own skill. At the top of this hierarchy is the Marquis who ostensibly is granted authority by the Royarch in Bretonnia, though it is likely it has been many years since the Lionheart has paid any mind to the troubles of Sontrailles, if at all. His rule is dynastic, failing that appointed by the predecessor. Beneath him are the counts, the lords who hold large tracts of land and rule at the pleasure of the Marquis and beneath them are barons who often rule towns with connected villages and hamlets and beneath the barons stand the earls, the rulers of towns and beneath the earls are petty lords. From the greatest city of Sontrailles to the small hamlet of ten families, each is ruled by a noble lord.

Not all nobles own land however, as many knights serve as household knights of a greater lord, and often these lords do not have enough land to grant or choose not to grant lands to them and rather grant lands to their male heirs. By technicality the children of nobles who are only in their errant phase of knighthood do not have noble titles at all, rather only earn them after they are elevated to knights of the realm. At this time should a knight be lucky enough to have a father who owns prodigious lands he can be granted a portion of it until such a time he succeeds his father, and often this is the case where the lands are split between the sons of a noble lord. Should the lord decide to take on the quest he relinquishes all lands and titles to his son until his return as a Knight of the Grail, or is granted Raven’s Wings by King Death. Sometimes if a noble son is brave enough he may wrest land from a rival power of Sontrailles, fighting in border wars with hired or loyal retinues so they may establish their own keeps. In this way Sontrailles has expanded over the years.

 Household knights by title do not own any land and serve as elite warriors of a noble and many intrepid sons of such knights may choose to become a knight bachelor, a knight without claim to land or allegiance to a lord. These knights do this to attract the attention of a lord of greater means in the chance that they may be recruited to his household and perhaps earn the right to land should their lord deem them worthy. Others do this for the chance at adventure. In any case knight bachelors are often amongst the most eager for battle in the field and often form units of their own on the battlefield. Most famous perhaps would be Guion le Brave, a knight bachelor who would become one of the founding members of the High Chivalric Order of the Shroud.

Most knights of Sontrailles can trace their lineage back to Bretonnian noble lineages with few exceptions, a marginal few claim nobility from old blood from other lands such as Tilea and Estalia. The honorable position of historian is among the highest a commoner may aspire to as it is their duty to keep records of noble lineages and heraldry, often sending underlings to Bretonnia to collect such information. The importance of their job is that many adventuring knights may become nobles within Sontrailles should the historians be able to back their claims, often they serve as household knights and earn their own titles. For a commoner to aspire would be foolhardy as though technically the Marquis himself could raise one to nobility, it simply is a rare occurrence. The one and only time this has happened is when Marquis Ramnulf de Naizon raised Giefferen granting the surname Durocher for his skill and ability to forge Virtuous Steel. For his efforts he was granted all rights and privileges of a noble, in fact Ademar Durocher swore vows of knighthood in 1517 and laid his life down valiantly at the Siege of Sontrailles in 1531.

entries.title: Heraldry
entries.body:
A noble’s family heraldry can often be traced over decades or centuries. This coat of arms is passed down through the ages through the bloodline and often influences a knight’s personal heraldry, for example the Marquis keeping the fleur-de-lys of Mousillon even when he changed his surname from his father’s. Blazons are typically added to personal heraldry to tell of great victories and accomplishments one might have achieved. Knights of Sontrailles ride into battle resplendent with heraldry, from his surcoat, tabard, pennant, shield, and lance all display his heraldic devices so that enemies and allies may recognize him. As a knight rises in rank from an errant to a knight of the realm or bachelor, their heraldry becomes more elaborate with marks of excellence, showing his higher status and greater prowess.

It is part of the role of historians to regulate the use of heraldic devices so that all noble knights may be recognized for their prowess in battle and great deeds. It is common for Sontrallais knights to bear their personal heraldry on their tabard or surcoat and their family heraldry on their shield, however inversions and exceptions exist.

entries.title: Culture
entries.body:
The roots of the Sontrallais undisputedly in Bretonnia, however more than a century later influences from Tilea, Estalia, the Empire, and Araby can be seen in the region. It is true that culturally the common man follows the norms of Bretonnia such that even though there are shrines to all of the classical gods, amongst them the Lady is venerated to a high degree, usurped by the worship of King Death, a title the Sontrallais call Morr. Indeed where the god Morr is mostly acknowledged and not necessarily worshipped as the patron in other parts of the Old World, King Death has become the most venerated amongst the gods in Sontrailles. While no regular rites are performed in worship the Groves of King Death always have some form of chapel or shrine while a great cathedral can be found in Sontrailles itself where one may pray for his aid. This worship of King Death has brought a unique outlook on death for the common man. The belief that it is celebrated rather than mourned, which brings about awkward conversations with funerary mourners within the cult. A common phrase “May sorrow not burden the dead” is common among the people when spoken of the dead or dying.

 The belief that human souls and only human souls are brought to King Death’s court after death brings an air of arrogance about the Sontrallais. Indeed the Sontrallais arrogance is so famous that it is said that a dwarf lord would rather deal with an elf prince than a noble of Sontrailles. It is well known that Sontrallais hold a prejudice towards those not of human origin, barking that feats of humanity far outstrip those of other races. Though one might scoff at such an idea many point to the feats of its greatest knights and ostentatiously brag about them, comparing them to the heroes of other lands, sometimes as if the feats were their own. Races such as ogres and gnomes and others are looked upon as tools to be used to the benefit of Sontrailles. That Sontrailles has survived more than a century in one form or another in the dangerous lands of the Border Princes is a point of pride, no doubt in their mind due to the skill of their knights. Those of Bretonnian blood see themselves as far superior to the others, and often live in streets and districts of their own, with landlords not allowing businesses nor tenancy without the proper heritage. Education is also relatively rare and usually reserved for those affluent enough to afford it.

The common people have a myriad of ways to expend energy and take time away from their woes. Sport games are rather popular among the low classe and high class and some believe it to be a bridge between the classes. The game of thrown-ball is popular, a game where a small ball of leather is taken and thrown to score hits on other players within a certain time limit, it has been known to cause brawls. The game of golf where a wooden rod is used to smack a ball into a pre determined dug hole or other form of container is also popular. Riding and all manner of tournaments bring the eyes of the common man away from their woes. Small wars are encouraged by the Marquis, where commoner soldiers are led by their liege lord of one town against another for glory and prizes, and mostly pride of their lord. Festivals will often have a competition of some sort, however segregation of the classes is to be expected. Every man is expected to have a duelling rapier or form of sword at their hip, as duelling is common in Sontrailles and disputes are often settled by them.

Sontrailles is also known for its lively ale and victualing houses which can be found all over the city but tend to concentrate nearest the gates. The mixture of alcohol and open discussion leaves keepers of these fine establishments understanding brawls are a foregone conclusion and will have patrons leave any weapons at the entrance with exception of those headed to upper floors of higher end establishments where manners are a matter of social contracts and minded and riffraff impolitely barred from. The Aubney Tree is a famous alehouse which has been a staple in the city. It has allowed commoners to speak openly of their betters for nearly a century. This venting is seemingly allowed as an outlet for the peasants to screech to their hearts content without the usual punishments involved though famously in 1552 dissidents actively threatened a rebellion and as soon as this was revealed to local authorities the patrons were subsequently clubbed to death and the proprietor hung over the Herwing’s Gate as an example to all. Tenancy of the establishment was then auctioned to the highest bidder.

There are a number of theaters in the city. Productions that are run originate from a variety of playwrights from Estalia, Tilea, and Bretonnia. The famous Sontrallais playwright Fracas is perhaps the most widely known in the region and a favorite of the locals. These theaters often have the nobility to thank for their patronage, those lords who believe themselves to be patrons of the arts and defenders of the nation. Some however spend for private boxes in the upper floor to remain distant from the smelly dirty peasants. The Opera House of Blue Roses is another attraction and symbol of great pride among the people. Everyone in the city has attended at least once in their lifetimes. When Clan Vordrit invaded and the ratmen threatened to storm the opera house during the performance of the beloved singer Elise, even the common man defended its steps, beating the ratmen with instruments.

entries.title: Festivals
entries.body:
L’aube: Also called the Dawn of Sontrailles Festival celebrates the founding of Sontrailles and theater productions show a dramatized account of the battle against the lichlord. Grand melee tournaments are held in the city for trophies and glory. On the second day productions of plays about the retaking of Sontrailles begin, and on this day all knights reaffirm their loyalty to Sontrailles by oath in full view of the commoners.
Festival of The Banners: Celebrated a week before the Spring Equinox and therefore the campaign season, a two day fair after which the Tournament of the Spurs is held for all knight errants to prove themselves before their seniors, a separate section is held for knight bachelors so they may too display their skills and earn commissions.
Week of Wines- Small festivals throughout the realm showcasing the various vintages and other drinks where all can enjoy good drink and good food in the late summer. Archery tournaments are held across the land.
Day of Honored Dead- on the day before Geheimnisnacht auguries are performed and dead relatives are honored. Hourglasses surrounded by candles are placed outside of homes to ward off evil spirits and honor relatives long past. In the morning any corrupted objects are burned.
La Nuit des Revenants - Also called Hexenacht by those who speak reikspiel. Most hide in their homes while the Raven Messengers and Grave Wardens conduct their rites. It is this day that the Honored Dead appear most frequently and do battle against cursed specters all through the night.
Day of Ashes- Celebrates the victory over the Lahmian vampires in Sonnental. A large procession begins from the foot of the hills and ends at Etienne’s Gate where great flames are lit and ashes scattered.
Shattered Lances and Shields Tournament- The final tournament in the season in late Autumn where knights compete in a joust, grand melee, single melee, and passage of arms. Prizes for each competition vary however should a knight errant win any he is elevated to knight of the realm.

Synod of the Raven’s Messengers

The cult of Mor found in Sontrailles is known as the Synod of the Raven’s Messengers and worship him as King Death. These adherents are not recognized by the Cult of Morr though they have sent representatives to the conclave in Luccini as the other sects believe they are far too spirited in their beliefs. The cultists of the Synod are indeed known to actively seek out the undead, more so than even templar orders of other sects. The Herald of King Death, the high priest of the cult, is one Denisot Pasteur, who urges his followers to destroy “any who would corrupt the soul” far and wide which usually include the ruinous powers. They are destroyed on sight. Graveyards are called Groves of King Death where black roses occasionally grow.

They believe that only human souls are allowed into the Court of King Death, believing the other races have their own patrons who look after them. It is believed that Morr as King Death rules a spectral kingdom more elevated than any kingdom in life and that nobles who die with honor in service to his designs or a chivalrous act will find their way to King Death’s court and serve within. Some say that the appearance of the Honored Dead is evidence enough, others say it is merely hearsay. Commoners however will not plow spectral fields in labor of their honorable lords however act as messengers, hearing the prayers of the living so that they may deliver them to the King himself. That is not to say that they may also appear as Honored Dead, but they must have been exceptional in life to appear so in death. Spectral ravens are rarely seen and are believed to be the messengers bringing back missives from the King in the form of dreams and visions. Those who prove themselves may be blessed and granted Raven Wings to succeed the missives sent by King Death himself. Signs of this are evident. The blessed man grows taller and stronger, his hair darkens, and his face becomes gaunt and his eyes pale. All are gifted witchsight to seek out those who would hide among the living and it is considered one of the first signs the person is favored by King Death. Ravens tend to follow those who are blessed by King Death, as the Keep of Deserved Rest and the cathedral draws ravens to them. Marquis Armand de Sontrailles is known to have a flock of ravens heralding his arrival on the battlefield and the realm.

There are two orders of priests in the cult, the Raven’s Messengers, and the Grave Wardens. The Messengers are those who stay and conduct the rites an ordinary Morrian priest would, granting final rites to the dead, auguries, warding against spirits, and the like. They train mourners to assist them and to minor consecrations of holy places of King Death such as graveyards and gravetending. Besides them are the Grave Wardens who are the warpriests of the cult, leading soldiers in battle and hunting villainous cultists. If the foe is too powerful for them and their band it is not uncommon for them to request aid from any of the knightly orders. They swear solemn oaths to face their enemies without fear and use divine magic to counter curses and hexes sent against them. They are armed well and carry their black lanterns which grant protection, strength, and illuminate their foes, showing them as they truly are. Soldiers who dip their weapons into the black lanterns imbued with its pale flames and themselves strengthened.

One of the most important duties of the cultists is the protection against vampires. It is widely believed that vampires cannot be truly destroyed without the direct intervention of the divine, such as King Death. Because of this a ritual binds a vampire into an object such as a personal item or their own bones so that they may never be resurrected again by their servants or foolhardy necromancers without that object. Once a vampire is defeated and burned bones are often taken, like a finger bone or skull, and this ritual is enacted upon it. These bones are protected in the vault of the High Chivalric Order of the Shroud, while some are collected as trophies by order members and displayed on their person as a challenge.

entries.title: Guilds and Industry
entries.body:
There are a great variety of guilds representing the skilled craftsmen and professional workers of all backgrounds in the realm. Guild membership is one avenue in which a person can attain citizenship, which means allowance of tenancy. The guilds offer apprenticeships and progression in their careers and other benefits ranging from pensions to a widow’s fund. These guilds also maintain certain standards such as quality and price and as such admittance is not always guaranteed. Guild leaders and members often police themselves and other members within the guild and often attempt to gain concessions from the lords by giving heavy gifts of coin in exchange for charters.

 Once admitted it is common for some form of badge of approval to be given, for example craftsmen typically are given an earring. Those in good standing can avail of all these benefits however those who lose their good standing by undercutting other members within the guilds can lose their membership and have their badges taken from them. These lowlifes are called “slit ears” or “patchworks” from the forcible removal of said badges.

Small list of guilds:

Brewers and Vintners Guild: Guild who regulates exports of spirits and wines and ensures quality as well as training of sommeliers
Glasswrights of Sainted Crystal: .
Butcher’s and Cooks: A growing group of professional cooks who maintain books of their recipes.
Powder Keg Boys: Guild of blackpowder weapon smiths and inventors whose patron is the Baron of Flumontel.
Physicians and Physik’s Guild: Guild of professional physicians attempting to standardize education, curatives, and procedures for the ill. Violently opposed to the Barber-Surgeon’s Guild.
Barber-Surgeon’s Guild: Those who would care for one’s hair and bloodletting at the same time. Scoffed at by their lack of apprenticeship and education by the Physician’s Guild.
Sailors and Cartographers: Those mariners who produce maps and refine sailing techniques and stevedores.
Leatherworkers Guild: Guild for tanners and those who work with leather..I mean what the fuck else are they.
Lawyers and Advocates Guild: While appealing to the court is nearly impossible it has not stopped some commoners from attempting to advocate for themselves and others.
Pigeon and other Bird Fanciers: Not as much as a guild but a club of those who fancy feathered birds and meet to converse with one another and show off their birds. It is rumored the Marquis himself is a member but rarely attends, having a multicolored bird akin to a mango named after an Arabyan princess.

Mining represents the oldest and most important component of the Sontraillais economy. The region contains substantial deposits of silver, iron, lead, copper, and quartz, with the silver workings of Palinam being among the most productive and politically significant. Silver is commonly refined and assayed within the realm before export, allowing the government to tax its production and maintain standards of weight and purity. Iron ore is likewise generally processed locally, as the export of finished iron and steel goods. The hills and mountains of the region are home to high quality iron for the forge. Sontraillais smiths produce tools, agricultural implements, and components for armor, much of which is sold throughout the Border Princes and neighboring lands.

Closely associated with the mining industry is the widely famous Sontraillais glass trade. The quartz deposits of the Geistenmund Hills provide much of the silica required by the region's glasshouses, while finer sands, soda ash, pigments, and other specialized materials are imported through southern trade routes, particularly from Araby and Tilea. Over time, local craftsmen developed a considerable reputation for glassblowing, glazing, mirror-making, and most famously the manufacture of stained and decorative glass. Among the most prestigious products are dark violet or black funerary glass associated with the cult of King Death, fine mirrors backed with locally mined silver, clear luxury glassware, alchemical vessels, and architectural panes. Glass production consequently supports numerous subsidiary trades.Pastoral agriculture forms an important secondary branch of the economy. Sheep are extensively raised upon the upland pastures, providing foodstuffs and textile goods, while hardy horses and mules are bred for military, agricultural, mining, and caravan use. Quarrying is also widespread, with slate, limestone, and darker ornamental stones exported to nearby territories for roofing, fortifications, monuments, and funerary construction. Timber, pitch, resin, beeswax, and charcoal are produced from surrounding woodland, although the demands of furnaces and glasshouses have made the regulation of foresting an increasing concern.

Sontrailles is not entirely self-sufficient in food. Its valleys support the cultivation of barley, rye, oats, vegetables, and fodder crops, but wheat and other staple grains are frequently imported, particularly in years of poor harvest. The realm therefore relies upon the export of high-value goods such as silver, steelwork, and luxury glass to finance the import of bulk necessities. Much of the imported wheat and foodstuffs come from Averland, Kreutzhofen, and Araby.

A further source of wealth is Sontrailles' position upon a major overland caravan route linking western and southern markets with lands farther east. Customs duties, road tolls, bridge fees, market dues, warehouse charges, and caravan licenses provide substantial revenue to the Marquisal government. Merchants traveling under officially recognized passes may also pay for protection along guarded roads and through fortified crossings. As a result, Sontrailles profits not only from the sale of its own goods, but also from the movement of foreign merchandise through its territory.

entries.title: Law
entries.body:
The rule of law is enforced by a particular group of city guardsmen most often led by members of the High Chivalric Order of the Scales. Their justiciars are charged with keeping the peace in the land. High ranking members serve as judges and dispense judgement in quick fashion. There are separate courts, one for commoners and one for nobles. The High Court, as the noble’s court is known as, is presided by senior members of the order and cases brought before them are known to take quite some time. The Low Court is presided over by younger members. It is noted there are no juries. High Court cases may be appealed to the appellate court though it is rarely done so. Those of any class that have the audacity to appeal to the Marquis himself will often find themselves facing their opponent in single combat.

Duels are a part of life in Sontrailles and as such are legal. They cannot however cause property damage or injure non-affiliated parties and they may not end in death with exception. Those found causing harm to others outside of the duel may find themselves arrested and beaten by local guardsmen or justiciars before being released in a closed arena to finish their duel.

Blackpowder weapons are legal in a way. Commoners are able to appeal for a charter from their local lord. For military necessity lords will grant these charters for his military dues so that his men at arms are able to wield those weapons in combat. Artillerymen are considered among the highest station men at arms are able to aspire to.

Violent criminals generally do not receive trial if they are of the lowborn regardless of wealth and punished in increasingly violent manners. First time offending thieves are beaten and their arms broken. Traitors and murderers are nearly strangled to death and then disemboweled. Rapists are impaled from the back end by a red hot iron rod until they expire. It is to be noted that the judges are fond of more imaginative ends the worse the crime is. Highborn are granted a full trial beforehand, and then if found guilty they are granted a more merciful death by practiced hands. Due to the very real threat of vampiric or undead attack curfews are set at eleven o’clock where stores must close and patrons must clear out. Those walking the streets at night must carry a torch to be easily identified, those who do not are beaten.

Legally commoners are not allowed to own land and stores but rather are tenants. Tenant farmers are higher than serfs, who must toil the land with little prospect. Tenancy is earned through coin payment or skilled labor in lieu of payment which allows for more freedoms. Wealthy commoners are able to appeal for charters allowing workshops to be built in towns which increases the wealth of the lord. Oftentimes the charters which normally have exorbitant fees are paid for by the lord if he believes the prospective tenant will increase his annual income and thus tax revenues. Some lords encourage workshops and other producers by lowering the taxes, so long as their own pockets are filled as a result.

Every man in the realm is obligated to train with some form of weapon with many choosing the bow. This is to ensure that should great peril arrive at Sontrailles' doorstep, every man is able to defend the realm proficiently as a levy. In addition every tenth household of a settlement no matter how large or small must produce one able bodied man to serve in the army of that settlement’s lord. In effect the smallest hamlet is of ten families, an area a knight who aspires to rule a holding must abide by regardless of future population loss.

entries.title: Knightly Orders
entries.body:
There are three knightly orders recognized in the realm of Sontrailles. Of the three two are religious and the last one is secular, dedicated to the enforcement of justice. The orders are open to all knights and with exception, commoners.

High Chivalric Order of the Shroud

The order was founded by the current Marquis and Grandmaster, Armand de Sontrailles, whose title is King Death’s Right Hand. This title stems from his zeal for enacting King Death’s will and striking down those who would corrupt and destroy the souls of mankind. Members are adherents to the morrian cult and the order is a templar order of the Synod of Raven’s Messengers. Noble members of the order are known as Knight Brethren, and must pass tests of chivalry and character to be admitted, this process may take up to a year ending in a final night in prayer in the castle chapel. For those commoners wishing to join the order a similar test of character and faith is administered before admittance. Those proven to be capable warriors may rise to the station of Sword Brethren, the professional commoner soldiers of the order who will lead a group of commoners or fight in units of their own.

The loremasters or librarians are those members who spend their days seeking information and researching the weaknesses and strengths of potential enemies. While the knights and sword brethren may be the symbols of martial prowess and earn glory in the field it is the librarians who pass the knowledge so that the warriors may succeed in the field and many are paladins themselves. Many of these librarians work closely with vampire slayer field agents so they may strike their targets down with efficiency. These Night Hounds are mostly commoners, and work in groups of underlings to root out the vampire and chaos menace. Its seat is the Sanctuary of Deserved Rest and hosts a small chapel to King Death in its courtyard. To join the elite inner circle one must succeed four quests with the final one slaying in single combat a vampire of note. This is taken to be a sign that King Death’s grace flows through the aspirant and that he is granted Raven Wings so that he may soar ever higher to meet the challenges he is expected to face.

Vows:

Forlorn Vow
Sable Vow
Raven’s Vow

High Chivalric Order of the Unbroken Spears

The order is made of justiciars who enforce the law. These men patrol settlements at the head of retinues and are decidedly separate from the town guard who work alongside them. Knight bachelors who choose to join must learn the law and pass a written exam before entry before they are admitted. While members typically own no land and there are no prospects for gaining land it is a steady stream of income with decidedly less risk of injury for the most part. Senior members are able to become judges and serve as judge, jury and executioner for cases with only one appellate court for appeals who mostly are inner circle members. It is a largely secular order, one dedicated to the law, however with the influences of Tilea, Verena is highly regarded within the order and many within the order dedicate themselves to her.

In the old days the lords of each settlement held court to preside over grievances and many still do; however the number of cases has necessitated this order. Sir Louis de Bruil is grandmaster of the order, though his title is “High Judge” rather than grandmaster. Their seat is in the Courthouse of Lain Street which is more like a small fortress than courthouse and serves as both prison and court. There is a separate group within the order known as the Dusk Watch who patrol the streets at night. Knights of this particular set carry silver mirrors as a way to identify vampires and are armed with silver edged weapons.

Vows:

Justice
Order
Generosity

High Chivalric Order of the Silver Lilies

The order is dedicated to the Lady of the Lakes and was founded by Godefroy de Cervellier who serves as its grandmaster. Their practices and traditions originate from the Cult of the Lady in Bretonnia and was founded as an opposite or counter to the Order of the Shroud, believing the waning influence of the Lady among the people of Sontrailles was a detriment. Order members serve in typical Bretonnian fashion with members taking the questing vow and departing for their quest for the grail. Lord Vortigern in the past was one of the few to succeed this quest as was Godefroy de Cervellier. The order recruits common soldiers from peasants tied to those lords who still venerate the lady though their training is decidedly not as thorough as their opposing order due to their reliance on nobility believing it was the Lady’s intent for nobility to act as both lance and shield of the people whose role was similar to that of the horse. Their seat is Aedric’s Rest which hosts the largest shrine in all of Sontrailles within its courtyard.

Those who quest and achieve greatness may earn the right to sit within the inner circle as do those who succeed and sup upon the grail.

Vows:

Knight’s Vow
Questing
Grail

entries.title: Military
entries.body:
The realm has endured decades of fraught with ork attacks and other perils amid the Border Princes, a testament to its strength. Every lord is compelled to train a personal retinue that they may call upon when defending his realm and may be called upon by the Marquis himself to march to war. Compared to the total populace, professional soldiers make up a small percentage but every man spends at least a few days every month to become proficient in combat. Most lords however train their populations in defensive combat aside from their professional soldiers and levies. Knights who do not serve as household knights each have their own retinues to add to the fighting forces of their liege lords.

The Marquis has a standing army of Sontrailles which serves as the realm’s fighting force and a personal corps which serves as his household soldiers. Among the populace household forces are the most well trained besides the knightly orders.

Among the soldiery stands the regiments of the Marquis’ Foreign Spears. This army is made up of debtors, prisoners, and foreigners who choose to serve for a period of five to ten years depending on the severity. Upon completion debtors and criminals are allowed to serve as serfs and have their sentences removed while serfs who choose to join may purchase tenant rights with any money earned from looting. The regiments are also a way for unskilled foreigners to earn citizenship of Sontrailles, hence the name. Should they complete their service they and their family are granted citizenship.

Knights and lords are required to pay for their own equipment and the equipment of their retinues with exceptions. The giants in service to Sir Andres de Bacque are armed and armored at the expense of the Marquis as he believes their strength is a powerful war time asset. Indeed wealthy commoners who have connections are able to assist their lords in this endeavor, paying for equipment and training for favors or special privileges unavailable to commoners. The siege towers and artillery are also paid for at the expense of local lords.

The knightly orders also must equip their own order forces and do so with order affiliated land revenue payment to the grandmasters with exception to the Order of the Scales who are almost entirely funded by the city of Sontrailles.

entries.title: Depths Watch
entries.body:
These handsomely paid individuals are hired to patrol mines, sewers, and tunnels of the realm. They are well armed with depth guns and hand weapons to counter any creatures found below. Undead are a common threat as are skaven and many days are spent in running battles with gutter runners. They may find skaven or other tunnels and are charged with dismantling them with charges after scouting the foreign tunnel and reporting back to watch commanders. Resupply camp are found in the tunnels, small camps where weary watchmen may take a brief respite and resupply before continuing their journey. They are paid dependent on the shift. A short shift is however long it takes for them to travel a preset of tunnels they are obligated to watch before returning to the surface. A long shift is how long it takes to reach an underground resupply camp and return the next day after their patrols are completed. It is a very dangerous job yet it is highly coveted as it is well paid. Squads of four are led by a more experienced watchman known as a Tunnel Wrecker, who has experienced dismantling skaven tunnels more than any person should in their lifetimes.

These men and women are the first line of defense against skaven incursions and sell their lives dearly so that local forces may prepare to mount a defense. Many die in the dark alone but their work is invaluable.

entries.title: Magic and Forging
entries.body:
School of the Arcane Prism

Estelle’s establishment of the School of the Arcane Prism was a great boon to Sontrailles’ power. Though most students are not even close to matching the skill and experience of the Colleges of Magic students, a handful have become magisters in their own right. Their abilities have allowed them to create defensive wards and other useful magics to assist in everyday life. They are trained to use Arabyan magic to aid their chosen lore, naturally most practice the Lore of Death due to Estelle’s affinity. Familiars aid them, most choosing elementals or djinn, by channeling the chosen wind and in this way the few magisters are able to use multiple winds of magic with some proficiency. To gain entrance into the school proficiency exams are required, and as a law those children, though extremely rare, must be trained through this school to protect the wider realm from the predations of daemons and arcane mishaps, that isn’t to say these still don’t happen from time to time.

Some students are charged with watching the natural leylines of the realm and learn from their mentors to monitor them. Most students congregate in Sontrailles as that is where the school is found, however many can be found traipsing across the realm, and even the Old World, with their mentors learning what they can. Some are charged with the dangerous task of collecting essence for the creation of more incarnate hourglasses in the form of the bones of monarchs or powerful beings such as dragons. These reagents are a necessity for the survival of Sontrailles as it is still believed that the Sons of the Kurgans will arrive in the future, and they must prepare. Estelle unleashed the power of an Incarnate Elemental of Death once against the powerful waaaugh of warlord Graod when they smashed their way through the River Trebleca.

Rune Carving

The skill of arms and armor manufacturing is left to the smiths. However Estelle’s and Talbot’s discoveries of magic infusion has allowed Sontrailles to fight with more powerful equipment. The simple rune magic mirrors the ability of the elves and dwarfs though no one has been able to fold all eight winds into a single rune without extreme damage or death as dwarfs are. In fact, folding more than one requires multiple rune carvers to work in tandem to fold the winds into the desired runes, so most only use one or two at a time. The runecarving forges are designed to direct the flow of the ambient winds of magic to easier ply their trade. Ammunition has also been infused with the winds of Death to great effect, trebuchets launching missiles that can route a company with a few well aimed shots or cannons that unleash such destruction that the enemy runs in fear.

Specific spells can be carved into the piece of equipment and because of this typically defensive spells are carved into armor and shields while offensive into weapons. It is well known that Nightbrandt, the weapon of the Marquis, has been infused with runes as well as an Incarnate Elemental of Death. Famously, runecarving was inspired by Bernajoux d’Grèmes’ weapon, Wind’s Roar, which was gifted by Sultan Kamil and said to have been enchanted with the power of the djinn.

The incorporation of runes into Virtuous Steel was a great marvel for the Durocher family, improving the alloy beyond what they believed was possible, even with Arabyan alchemy. The great lords of Sontrailles wear these runed Virtuous Steel harnesses and wield their powerful weapons on the field of battle.

Virtuous Steel

The famous Virtuous Steel is an alloy created by the traditions of the Durocher family. It is a secret jealously guarded by their family, understandably so, for should any other prove better their privileges may wane. Some wild theories abound that the metal is formed by alchemical or magical means. All that is truly known however is that it is an alloy of quality steel and the Durocher family unequivocally state that it is nothing more. Some assistants have been kidnapped to be questioned, however for some reason they would rather die than divulge their secrets, even when tempted with exorbitant amounts of coin. For whatever reason the assistants of the Durocher family have remained loyal, some suspect threats and intimidation.

As production is limited a single suit of armor is extremely costly as is a weapon. It is tradition for knight errants to earn the right to wear and wield such equipment by being elevated to knights of the realm and so even though they ride to war with quality steel, it is not the same as a suit of Virtuous Steel. Both orders commission suits and weapons from the Durocher family. In fact it is a sign of prestige to field entire lances of knights equipped with Virtuous Steel. Because runecarving is also costly it is uncommon for household knights to be able to procure such equipment. The knights of the Marquis ride to war in full suits wield weapons of Virtuous Steel and their steeds are harnessed in barding of the metal.
